audits.ideal: Every fan-out endpoint in the dashboard API carries a named degraded flag when any source fails, and every pixel that could assert calm — verdict openers, all-clear strips, KPI zeros, empty states, liveness badges, stacked charts — reads that flag before rendering, so a partial outage is visually distinct from a genuinely quiet system on all ~12 aggregation surfaces, not just the four renderers named in the epic bead. The honesty contract is closed-loop: a flag the backend emits with zero frontend readers is treated as a build failure (a registry/coverage test enumerates emitted degraded fields and asserts at least one consumer), and honesty primitives like LiveStatusBadge's isDown are adopted by every surface that renders them, not just the one that motivated the fix.
audits.jarvis_gap: The 07-04 moves 1 and 2 are substantially real: the DegradedSources tracker exists and is threaded through all seven named routers, the board/system/notifications/settings/secrets/spend-summary/plex consumers genuinely read their flags and suppress all-clear, and six of the seven fabrication hotfixes are present and honest on main. But the epic's own boundary — 'gate the four named renderers' — left a ring of emitted-but-unread flags where the backend now tells the truth and no pixel listens: memory's pools_failed has zero consumers (the /memory 'is remembering working' verdict still fabricates calm over a half-failed fan-out), spend's daily/top-sessions/breakdown flags are dropped on the floor, approvals' sources_degraded remains unread (known, bu-enep6, though that bead is now two-thirds stale), and the timeline isDown fix stopped one page short of the badge's original home on the ingestion ledger. The gap between today and the ideal is no longer 'the backend fabricates calm' — it is that honesty flags can ship as backend-only artifacts and count as done.

findings.title: NEW TAXONOMY SHAPE: gate ships, burn-down never burns — a completeness gate lands with the entire surface grandfathered into its skip manifest, and the gate's existence is then cited as coverage
findings.detail: Move 10's 'registry-driven axe sweep' is a completeness CHECK, not axe coverage: route-sweep.a11y.test.tsx asserts every ALL_ROUTES path is either covered elsewhere or skip-listed. The mechanism is internally honest ('burn-down list, NOT a gate-blocker; the vast majority of routes start in the skip manifest') but the epic-level claim 'registry-driven axe sweep' reads as coverage delivered when zero new pages gained an axe pass. This shape deceives the owner/auditor reading the changelog rather than the end user, and fits none of shapes 1-12 (which are all runtime-UI deceptions): the Tell is a quality gate whose exemption manifest at ship time contains ~100% of the surface, with no follow-up bead to retire entries. Fix posture: every gate-with-manifest ship must carry a burn-down bead (or a max-manifest-size ratchet) or be described as 'ledger', not 'sweep'.

audits.ideal: Every shared mechanism shipped by the Dispatch/verdict/choreography/shortcut moves is the ONLY implementation of its contract: one heading voice (Title/Display) reaching every H1 whether or not the page uses the Page shell; one identity-hue registry covering every agent that can appear on the board, staffers included, with zero collisions by construction; one verdict primitive whose sources include not just transport errors but every degraded-envelope flag the backend already emits, so a partial fan-out failure can never render as calm; one modal-choreography contract applied to every element carrying role=dialog, enforced structurally (lint or axe) rather than by memory; and quality gates whose skip manifests are born with a burn-down owner so 'sweep' means shrinking exemptions, not a permanent ledger of them.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today the four moves are genuinely real and broadly adopted — the primitives exist, are tested, and adoption did not stop at 1-3 consumers (5 verdict openers all rendered, 4 modal-choreography overlays, 4 useListTriage lists, ~15 palette-verb surfaces, aliased tokens in both themes) — but the seams leak exactly where the doctrine matters most: the approvals verdict can say 'No approvals waiting' while a butler pool is down because the backend's own sources_degraded flag has no frontend reader; the chat widget promises a dialog it doesn't keyboard-honor; switchboard silently wears lifestyle's identity hue on the five-second-verification board; the axe 'sweep' added a completeness gate but zero new coverage; and both extraction origins (SystemVerdictBanner, ingestion EventDrawer) still run parallel hand-rolled copies of the contracts extracted from them.

findings.title: NEW TAXONOMY SHAPE: half-wired dual-channel liveness — a query claims bus+poll layering but only one channel is attached
findings.detail: Move 14 codifies a two-channel liveness contract: a live surface is updated by the event bus (primary) AND a POLL_BUS_RECONCILE_MS sweep (safety net when the bus is down). Either channel can be silently missing and the surface still looks live. Direction A (poll demoted, bus never wired) was the proven notifications gap the coverage manifest fixed. Direction B is live NOW: use-notifications.ts hooks (useNotifications/useNotificationStats/useButlerNotifications) gained bus coverage via notificationPatch but have NO refetchInterval at all — a bus outage freezes the notifications list/stats until a window-focus refetch, unlike every sibling hook (sessions/approvals/spend/timeline/board) which pairs bus coverage with the reconcile token. Distinct from shape 8 (component states) and shape 11 (multi-source join): the deception lives in the update plumbing of a single healthy-looking query. Tell: diff the set of hooks in EVENT_CACHE_COVERAGE_MANIFEST against the set using POLL_BUS_RECONCILE_MS — any asymmetric member has only one channel. The coverage test cannot catch this: it verifies only manifest opt-ins ('invisible to this test by design', its own header), so the guard's scope is the claimant's list.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-notifications.ts:26-56 (three useQuery calls, zero refetchInterval) vs frontend/src/hooks/use-sessions.ts:46 and use-timeline.ts:28 (POLL_BUS_RECONCILE_MS safety net); frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-registry.ts:128-135 (notificationPatch invalidates them); frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-registry.coverage.test.ts:16-20 (opt-in scope disclaimer)

findings.title: Daily insight delivery cycle is crashing in production on insight_cooldowns pkey collision
findings.detail: record_cooldowns() does a plain INSERT into insight_cooldowns (pkey = dedup_key) with no ON CONFLICT. The pending filter only excludes dedup_keys with cooldown_until > now, but expired cooldown rows are retained until cleanup_old_rows' retention window — so a candidate redelivered after its cooldown lapses collides with its own stale row. The crash happens AFTER candidates are marked delivered (broker.py:1025) but BEFORE the attention-ledger delivered/coalesced rows (broker.py:1047), engagement recording, and cleanup — so delivered insights go unledgered and cleanup is skipped, and the whole daily job records an error. Live: switchboard.scheduled_tasks 'insight-delivery-cycle' last_result = duplicate key (dedup_key relationship:entity-dedup:53fe...) at 2026-07-10 00:07; health has 5 expired candidates never delivered. Fix: ON CONFLICT (dedup_key) DO UPDATE SET cooldown_until/reason.
findings.evidence: roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py:483-487 (plain INSERT, no ON CONFLICT), :298 (filter only on cooldown_until > $1), :1025-1057 (delivered-mark precedes cooldown insert precedes ledger rows); live: SELECT last_result FROM switchboard.scheduled_tasks WHERE name='insight-delivery-cycle' → {"error": "duplicate key value violates unique constraint \"insight_cooldowns_pkey\" ... Key (dedup_key)=(relationship:entity-dedup:...)"} at 2026-07-10 00:07:17

findings.title: NEW TAXONOMY SHAPE: benign-branch-only ledger — an honesty ledger whose writers cover only the non-error branches, so the durable record itself misattributes the failure mode
findings.detail: attention_ledger.py's contract says 'a notification is never silently dropped: it is recorded as delivered, coalesced, deferred, or suppressed'. But secrets_lifecycle records a ledger row on the suppressed branch (line 328), the deliver-returned-failed branch (line 371), and the delivered branch (line 385) — while the no-recipient branch (lines 342-349) and the generic-exception branch (lines 407-411) record NOTHING. Because the live failure is an exception (UndefinedTableError), the ledger's only story for this source is '120 quiet-hours suppressions' — a systematically biased narrative that makes a 100%-broken delivery path look like a strict-but-working attention policy. Distinct from taxonomy shape 11 (frontend multi-source join) and shape 2 (UI success toast): the deception lives in the durable back-end record that downstream consumers/audits will trust. Tell: enumerate every terminal branch of the instrumented path and diff against the ledger-writer call sites; any except/early-return branch without a writer is a silent-drop hole. Same hole in the insight broker: a crash between delivered-mark and ledger write (the live cooldown crash) leaves delivered insights unledgered.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/attention_ledger.py:21-24 (contract); src/butlers/jobs/secrets_lifecycle.py:342-349 (no-recipient: errors+=1, continue, no record_attention_event), :407-411 (except: errors+=1, no record); live bias: 120 suppressed / 0 anything-else for a path that is actually crashing every awake-hours run

findings.title: Approval preview shows the 3 newest, not 3 soonest-expiring, approvals; the 'N more' collapse row is unreachable dead code; per-pool degradation invisible
findings.detail: usePendingApprovalsFlat(3) sends limit=3 server-side (DashboardPage.tsx:112; client.ts:3540-3548) and the flat endpoint truncates after ORDER BY requested_at DESC (approvals.py:1537-1554), so byExpirySoonFirst (model.ts:417-421,434) sorts only within the server's newest-3 — the soonest-expiring approval fleet-wide can be permanently absent from the pane whose sort contract implies expiry priority. Because fetch cap == display cap (maxAttentionApprovalRows=3), remaining = sorted.length - shown.length is always 0, so the designed '<N> more pending approvals' row (model.ts:446-456) can never render from this caller. The endpoint's DegradedSources meta (approvals.py:1533,1550) is also never read, so a failed butler pool's approvals silently vanish from the actionable rows. Additionally every approval row hardcodes severity 'medium' (model.ts:439) and the expiry driving the sort is never rendered as a clause on the row.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/DashboardPage.tsx:112; frontend/src/api/client.ts:3540-3548; src/butlers/api/routers/approvals.py:1537-1554; frontend/src/components/overview/model.ts:417-421,434-456,439

findings.title: Attention list has no cross-kind severity ordering — at 3am a crashed butler sorts below up to five issue rows
findings.detail: attentionRows is a fixed kind-order concatenation: source-error, current-high issues (max 5), runtime, approvals, notifications, qa, recent issues (model.ts:204-212). A runtime 'offline' row carries severity 'high' (model.ts:404) and 'QA patrol failed' carries 'high' (model.ts:620-624), yet both always render after every current-high issue row and (for QA) after medium approvals/notifications. The incident-first reading order the page promises ('operational triage cockpit') is not what the list delivers when it matters most.

findings.title: Sessions·24h KPI is a zero-fallback with no degraded marker, and computes a different number than /butlers' same-named aggregate

audits.ideal: The ideal Overview is the one pane where five seconds and zero keystrokes answer "is my household staff healthy, and what needs me?" with a single, provable verdict: the opening headline, the KPI strip, the attention list, and the butler index all derive from ONE composed fleet model (canonical board verdict + issues + approvals + notification pressure + QA breaker) so the prose can never contradict the evidence beneath it; every degraded upstream — a 200-with-zeros envelope as much as a failed fetch — surfaces as a named partial-visibility clause ("registry unreachable — health counts partial") rather than a calm zero, so at 3am a dead daemon reads as the top row in red, ordered by severity across kinds, with the crashed butler's door one Enter away and its dossier one more; approval rows are ranked by real urgency (expiry fleet-wide, risk tier), render their expiry and blast-radius clause inline, and remain undoable one-keystroke decisions; and every clause on the page — each KPI digit, each activity line, each briefing sentence — is a door carrying its own predicate onto the trace spine (filtered timeline, session dossier, butler detail), so verification and investigation are the same motion.

moves.title: One attention model: classify the briefing from the same composed verdict the page renders, with a degraded-honesty flag
moves.why: vision.md 'The system is boring. It works.' requires the page's opening sentence to be trustworthy; purpose-and-single-pane.md Detect loop; bu-qvnce.4 unified KPI+attention+board on one verdict but the headline still runs a third private model (dashboard_briefing.py:290-344,393-400) that says 'busy' over 'Nothing waiting.' and 'All quiet.' during fetch failures. Payoff: the five-second verdict becomes provable — headline count == attention-list count by construction.

Payoff: earned calm — partial outages footnote themselves exactly as /butlers, /notifications, /spend already do.

audits.jarvis_gap: Today /butlers is a genuinely consolidated status board (single /api/butlers/board round trip, canonical server-side verdict, needs-you strip, degraded-source notes) and the detail page is one coherent console with a unified command bar — but the surface still lies about its own freshness (header claims 30s refresh while the query reconciles every 5 minutes and non-session transitions have no bus event), consequential actions (restore/pause) succeed in a toast while the verdict chips stay stale for up to 5 minutes, the header pill and the needs-you strip compute "healthy" from different sets and can contradict each other on the same screen, and the butler-detail Overview quietly fabricates calm ($0.00 spend on a failed source, flat zero stripe when the same butler's board cell says "data unavailable", a status dot whose green/red tones are unreachable because the FE branches on a vocabulary the endpoint never emits). Keyboard triage and palette verbs, now standard on dashboard/issues/notifications, skipped this surface entirely.

findings.title: Board header fabricates freshness: claims 'refreshes every 30s' while the query polls every 5 minutes
findings.detail: ButlersPage passes REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS=30_000 to BoardHeader purely as a caption, but useButlersBoard() actually uses refetchInterval: POLL_BUS_RECONCILE_MS = 5*60_000. The bus only invalidates ["butlers","board"] on session started/ended events — a butler going offline (MCP probe fail), being auto-quarantined, or tipping overdue produces NO bus event, so those verdict transitions surface only at the 5-minute reconcile while the header asserts 30-second freshness. The event-cache-registry comment ('not on its next 30s poll') is stale too. The fleet-verification surface — the one the vision says must be trustworthy in five seconds — is up to 10x staler than it claims.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/ButlersPage.tsx:46 (REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS=30_000, comment: 'forwarded to BoardHeader's refresh caption'); frontend/src/components/butlers/BoardHeader.tsx:79-83 (refreshLabel rendered); frontend/src/hooks/use-butlers.ts:58 (refetchInterval: POLL_BUS_RECONCILE_MS); frontend/src/lib/poll-policy.ts:23 (= 5*60_000); frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-registry.ts:100-115 (only sessionPatch touches ["butlers","board"]); event-cache-registry.ts:84 stale '30s poll' comment

findings.title: Restore/Pause eligibility mutation never invalidates the board — cell shows QUARANTINED up to 5 min after the 'restored' toast
findings.detail: useSetEligibility onSuccess invalidates only ["switchboard-registry"]. The board query (["butlers","board"]) and hence the StatusBoardCell chip, the eligibility rail, the needs-you strip, and the ButlerDetailHeader activity chip are untouched. After the undo window elapses and fireRestore toasts '<name> restored', the cell keeps rendering QUARANTINED/red until the 5-minute reconcile poll (no bus event fires for eligibility changes). Same for Pause/Resume on the detail page: the Actions pill flips (it reads useRegistry) while the header chip one line above stays 'quarantined'. Success feedback contradicted by the visible verdict (failure-taxonomy shape 2 adjacent).
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-general.ts:57-59 (onSuccess invalidates only ["switchboard-registry"]); frontend/src/pages/ButlersPage.tsx:133-144 (fireRestore toasts success); frontend/src/hooks/use-butlers.ts:52-58 (board key + 5-min interval); frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-registry.ts:100-115 (no eligibility event type)

findings.title: Detail Overview status dot is always dim: FE branches on a status vocabulary GET /api/butlers/{name} never emits (shape 12)
findings.detail: statusTone() handles 'ok'/'healthy'→green, 'degraded'/'waiting'→amber, 'error'/'down'→red, else dim. But the detail endpoint's _get_live_status returns only 'online'|'offline', and ButlerOverviewTab computes `status = butler?.status ?? row?.status` where butler.status always wins post-load. So a healthy butler renders a DIM grey dot (not green) and a crashed butler renders the SAME dim dot (not red) — the tone axis is entirely dead in production. The unit-test fixture uses status:'ok' (a value the endpoint cannot emit), so tests pass while production behavior differs — the stale-fixture trap MEMORY.md already warns about, in a new spot.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/butler-detail/ButlerOverviewTab.tsx:45-50 (statusTone branches), :274 (butler?.status ?? row?.status); src/butlers/api/routers/butlers.py:1026-1037 (_get_live_status returns 'online'/'offline' only), :880,890 (detail.status = that value); frontend/src/components/butler-detail/ButlerOverviewTab.test.tsx:58,85 (fixtures use status:'ok')

findings.title: Detail Overview fabricates calm on degraded sources: '$0.00 today' on failed spend source, flat zero stripe when the board cell says 'data unavailable'
findings.detail: ButlerOverviewTab: (a) costToday = spendSummary.by_butler[name] ?? 0 — renders a confident '$0.00' KpiCell when the spend query errored (only isLoading is branched, not isError) or when the butler is listed in SpendSummary.unavailable_butlers, which is consumed nowhere on this page (grep: only SpendPage reads it). ButlerDetailHeader on the SAME page uses `?? null` → '--', so header and overview disagree about the same fact. (b) stripe = row?.hourlyStripe ?? Array(24).fill(0) and the render ignores row.hourlyStripeError — when a butler's schema is unreachable, its board cell honestly says 'data unavailable' while its own detail Overview shows a calm all-zero 24h stripe (shape 11: failure degrades to benign). sessions24h likewise falls to 0.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/butler-detail/ButlerOverviewTab.tsx:270 (?? 0), :313-321 (only isLoading branched), :273 (zero-fill fallback), :334 (ActivityStripe rendered without hourlyStripeError gate); grep 'unavailable_butlers' → only frontend/src/pages/SpendPage.tsx:1406-1483; contrast frontend/src/components/butler-detail/ButlerDetailHeader.tsx:47-51,119 (?? null → '--'); contrast frontend/src/components/butlers/StatusBoardCell.tsx:324-333 ('data unavailable' branch)

findings.title: Header pill and needs-you strip compute 'healthy' from different sets — green '11/11 reporting' above '2 things need you'
findings.detail: BoardHeader.healthyCount = total - offline - quarantined, and the pill goes green when healthy===total && !sourcesPartiallyDegraded. But the canonical needs-attention set (NEEDS_YOU_ACTIVITIES, exported precisely so 'every consumer classifies from the exact same set') includes 'overdue' and per-row 'unknown'. Overdue butlers trip neither the pill math nor sourcesPartiallyDegraded, so the pill shows a fully-green fleet directly above a strip listing overdue butlers needing the owner. Bonus axis mislabel: 'reporting' — quarantined butlers DO report (they answer ping); the pill's word and its math describe different things.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/butlers/BoardHeader.tsx:36-38 (healthyCount omits overdue/unknown), :50-55 (pillDotClass); frontend/src/hooks/use-butler-status-board.ts:179-192 (NEEDS_YOU_ACTIVITIES incl. overdue+unknown, with the 'exact same set' comment); src/butlers/api/routers/butlers.py:755-757 (overdue not in sources_partially_degraded)

findings.title: Pause/Resume is instant, silent on failure, and asymmetric with the board's undoable restore
findings.detail: handlePauseToggle fires the eligibility mutation with no onSuccess/onError callbacks: a failed pause produces no toast, no message — the button label just reverts, indistinguishable from success at a glance (missing-states, shape 8). Pausing a butler is consequential (it stops running), yet it fires instantly, while the board's restore of the SAME eligibility field earned a 5s undo window (ButlersPage RESTORE_UNDO_WINDOW_MS). One field, two verbs, two safety models.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/butler-detail/ButlerDetailActions.tsx:143-149 (mutate with no callbacks); frontend/src/pages/ButlersPage.tsx:52,146-162 (undo-window restore for the same mutation); frontend/src/hooks/use-general.ts:54-60 (no error handling in hook either)

findings.title: Dead per-row-stagger residue: hourlyStripeLoading is hardcoded false, its skeleton branches and aria fallback are unreachable
findings.detail: Since the single-round-trip consolidation, mapRow sets hourlyStripeLoading: false unconditionally ('Always false: the board loads in one round trip'). StatusBoardCell still carries two Skeleton branches and an aria-label branch (`hourlyStripeLoading ? sessions24h : ...`) keyed on it — all dead code, and the only board-surface consumer of StatusBoardRow.sessions24h is that dead branch. Zero-compat doctrine says delete the field and branches.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-butler-status-board.ts:67-68,168 (always false); frontend/src/components/butlers/StatusBoardCell.tsx:189 (dead aria branch), :279-281 and :322-323 (dead Skeleton branches)

findings.title: Two different 'sessions in 24h' numbers for the same butler on adjacent screens
findings.detail: The board cell's SESS 24H shows hourly_total (sum of the stripe query); the detail Overview's sessions panel shows sessions_24h (a separate query_sessions_24h read-model). Both are real, but they are computed by different SQL over different bucketing and can disagree — the owner drills from a cell reading N into a panel reading M for the same fact. One fact should have one number (the board row already carries both fields).

audits.ideal: The ideal /butlers is the household's five-second muster: one glance at a header whose pill, strip, and grid all derive from the single exported needs-attention set, with a freshness caption that states what is literally true ("live via event bus, reconciled 12s ago") because every verdict-changing transition — session start/end, eligibility change, probe down, overdue tick — emits a bus event that flips the affected cell within a beat. Every consequential verb (restore, pause, run) is undoable or confirmed, reflects optimistically in the cell it changes, and reports failure as loudly as success; every number on a cell reappears identical on the detail page or is a door to the evidence that explains the difference. The butler detail Overview is the board cell magnified — same status vocabulary, same degraded-source honesty ("spend source unavailable", "activity data unavailable"), never a fabricated $0.00 or flat stripe — and the whole surface is keyboard-native: j/k across cells, Enter to open, r to restore the focused quarantined butler, palette verbs for every needs-you item.

findings.title: Sessions endpoints skipped the honest-aggregation sweep — partial DB outage renders as all-clear or 'Session not found'
findings.detail: Every cross-butler sessions read (list, aggregate, trigger breakdown, detail-by-id) uses the silent DatabaseManager.fan_out(), which swallows per-butler pool failures and returns an empty list for the failed butler. fan_out_with_status() exists expressly for the fleet degraded convention (bu-qvnce.1) but the sessions router/read-model never call it, and KeysetMeta/ApiResponse carry no degraded flag. Consequences on the busiest trace-spine hub: (a) the verdict opener declares 'No sessions failed in the last 24h' when the failing butler's DB is the unreachable one — fabricated calm at the exact moment of an incident; (b) the KPI strip undercounts silently; (c) the list omits a butler's sessions with no indication; (d) GET /api/sessions/{id} returns 404 'Session not found' for a session that exists but whose butler pool is down — failure impersonating absence for the 10+ surfaces that deep-link here (spend, approvals, timeline, notifications, palette post-trigger nav). The frontend's per-query isError plumbing (SessionsPinnedStrip, DispatchVerdict sources) only sees whole-request failures, so it cannot compensate.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/read_models/sessions_v1.py:373, 443, 514, 545 (all four fan-outs call db.fan_out); src/butlers/api/db.py:242-247 ('If a query fails... empty list and the error is logged') vs db.py:249-268 (fan_out_with_status, unused by sessions); src/butlers/api/routers/sessions.py:368-374 (KeysetMeta has no degraded field), :495-496 (row None -> 404); frontend/src/components/sessions/SessionsVerdictOpener.tsx:78-83 (all-clear text built from the aggregate)

findings.title: Drawer butler-resolution breaks for pinned rows and ?selected deep links — 'This session could not be loaded' for real sessions
findings.detail: SessionsPage resolves the drawer's butler solely from the current 20-row table page: sessions.find(s => s.id === selectedSessionId)?.butler ?? ''. Pinned-strip rows come from separate unfiltered queries (running: no page filters; failures: 24h window), so whenever a pinned session is not in the current table page (any active butler/status filter, any deep cursor, or >20 newer sessions), butler resolves to '' and useSessionDetail is disabled (enabled: !!butler). A disabled query has isLoading=false and no data, so SessionDetailDrawer renders the hard error branch 'This session could not be loaded. It may not exist or the butler may be unavailable.' The same happens on every ?selected= deep-link/reload while the list is fetching (flash) and permanently when the session is off page 1. The fix is also a cruft removal: useGlobalSessionDetail (GET /api/sessions/:id) already exists and is what SessionDetailPage uses; the butler-scoped drawer path (and its parallel cache key that useSessionErrorExcerpts primes) is a second detail spine for no reason.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/SessionsPage.tsx:288-289 (butler from table rows only), :514-521 (pinned rows share the same selectSession); frontend/src/hooks/use-sessions.ts:87-96 (enabled: !!butler && !!id); frontend/src/components/sessions/SessionDetailDrawer.tsx:57-65 (isError || (!isLoading && !session) -> hard error copy); frontend/src/hooks/use-sessions.ts:109-116 (global endpoint already exists)

findings.title: The 'streaming tool-call tail' for running sessions is structurally impossible — tool_calls is only written at completion
findings.detail: use-sessions.ts documents POLL_RUNNING_SESSION_MS as 'the primary path for a running session's streaming tool-call tail', and the dossier polls a running session every few seconds. But the backend writes sessions.tool_calls exactly once, in session_complete(); during the run the column stays '[]', so the dossier renders 'Tool Calls (0) — No tool calls recorded.' for the session's entire lifetime — an affirmative false statement (calls HAVE run; the daemon captures them live in _captured_tool_calls) — then dumps everything at once on termination. Failure taxonomy shape 9: the poll implies a live axis the data layer never populates. The in-memory capture buffer (tool_call_capture.py) is the obvious source for a live tail: either periodic UPDATE flushes from the spawner or a daemon endpoint the dashboard API proxies for success IS NULL sessions.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-sessions.ts:21-34,93-95 (poll billed as the streaming tail path); src/butlers/core/sessions.py:236-304 (session_complete is the sole tool_calls writer, UPDATE at :287); src/butlers/core/tool_call_capture.py:26 (_captured_tool_calls in-memory buffer exists); frontend/src/components/sessions/ToolCallTimeline.tsx:286-289 ('No tool calls recorded.')

findings.title: Sessions cost column and dossier Token Usage silently exclude prompt-cache tokens — understated cost, inconsistent with Spend
findings.detail: The sessions table carries cached_input_tokens and cache_creation_tokens (written by session_complete), and estimate_session_cost supports cached_input_tokens/cache_creation_tokens kwargs — the 'prompt-cache pricing end-to-end' work. But sessions_v1's SUMMARY_COLUMNS and DETAIL_COLUMNS omit both cache columns, and _cost_usd_for_dto prices from input/output tokens only. Since input_tokens excludes cache reads by contract ('cache reads/writes are tracked separately'), the table's Cost column systematically understates cache-heavy sessions relative to the Spend page's cache-aware math, and the dossier's 'Token Usage' section (Input/Output/Total) presents a 'Total' that can be a small fraction of actual token traffic. A true number under a caption asserting a different axis (taxonomy shape 10) on the page the owner uses to answer 'what did this session cost'.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/sessions.py:247-248,296-297 (cache columns written; :265 'cache reads/writes are tracked separately'); src/butlers/api/read_models/sessions_v1.py:63-74 (SUMMARY_COLUMNS/DETAIL_COLUMNS lack cache columns); src/butlers/api/routers/sessions.py:180-197 (_cost_usd_for_dto: in_tok/out_tok only); src/butlers/api/pricing.py:306-315 (estimate_session_cost accepts cache kwargs, unused here); frontend/src/components/sessions/SessionDossier.tsx:311-324 (Token Usage = input+output only)

findings.title: Trigger filter is a free-text input over an exact-match predicate — partial text yields a false 'No sessions found'
findings.detail: The filter bar renders Trigger as a free-text Input ('Filter by trigger...'), but the backend applies trigger_source = $N exact equality. Typing 'sched' (for 'schedule') or any partial/differently-cased value returns zero rows, and the table then shows the generic empty state 'No sessions found. Sessions appear as butlers process triggers and scheduled tasks.' — misdiagnosing a filter mismatch as an idle fleet. trigger_source is a small closed-ish vocabulary the backend can already enumerate (aggregate by_trigger_source, /analytics/session-kinds); this should be a Select like Butler/Status. Compounding: the empty state never acknowledges active filters or offers 'Clear filters' (the button lives in a different card).
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/SessionsPage.tsx:411-426 (free-text Input); src/butlers/api/routers/sessions.py:119-121 (trigger_source = $idx exact match); frontend/src/components/sessions/SessionTable.tsx:111-119 (filter-blind empty state); src/butlers/api/read_models/sessions_v1.py:476-519 (distinct trigger_source breakdown already queryable)

findings.title: 'To' date filter excludes the selected day, and the stripe chart on the same page disagrees with the table about the same filter
findings.detail: The To filter is <input type='date'> producing 'YYYY-MM-DD'; the client passes it raw as to_date and the backend applies started_at <= to_date, i.e. midnight at the START of the chosen day — so 'To: 2026-07-10' excludes essentially all of July 10. Meanwhile SessionStripeChart's parseFilterDate anchors a date-only until to 23:59:59.999Z. Result: with From=To=today, the chart above the table shows today's sessions while the table below it is empty — two components on one page rendering contradictory answers to the same filter, and the user's natural reading ('inclusive day') matches the chart, not the table.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/SessionsPage.tsx:483-497 (type='date' inputs); frontend/src/api/client.ts:652-655 (raw pass-through since->from_date, until->to_date); src/butlers/api/routers/sessions.py:137-139 (started_at <= to_date); frontend/src/components/dashboard/session-stripe-utils.ts:133-141 (until anchored to end-of-day 23:59:59.999Z)

findings.title: Retry lineage and correction_count are fetched by the backend on every detail request and dropped by the frontend
findings.detail: GET session detail selects retry_attempted, retry_succeeded, result_source, attempt_count from session_process_logs and runs a count(*) on corrections to attach correction_count — but the FE SessionDetail type omits correction_count entirely and its process_log type omits all four retry fields, and no component renders them (taxonomy shape 5: backend-ready, frontend-not-wired). The dossier's header comment claims it 'Renders EVERY SessionDetail field the store holds', which is now false: a failed-then-retried session's dossier never says its result came from attempt 2, and a session the owner corrected shows no trace of the correction. Each detail request pays the corrections count(*) for a value nobody can see.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/sessions.py:255-279 (retry fields + correction_count fetched); frontend/src/api/types.ts:232-262 (SessionDetail/process_log: no correction_count, no retry fields); frontend/src/components/sessions/SessionDossier.tsx:12-30 ('Renders EVERY SessionDetail field' claim); grep retry_attempted|attempt_count|result_source|correction_count over frontend/src -> only types absent, zero render sites

findings.title: The trace spine walks up but not down: no child-sessions door, and no session-to-audit door
findings.detail: SessionDossier links parent_session_id to the parent's dossier, but there is no way to ask 'what sessions did this one spawn' — _build_where has no parent_session_id predicate, SessionParams has no parent filter, and the dossier has no Children section. A Switchboard routing session that fanned out to domain butlers shows its parent link on each child but the parent shows nothing. Separately, the vision's spine (signal -> session -> audit -> root evidence) has no session->audit segment: public.audit_log has no session_id column (writer maps butler/operation/target/metadata only) and the audit router filters on actor/action/key/result/kind/since — so from a session dossier the owner cannot see the audited actions that session performed, nor from an audit row jump to its session.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/sessions/SessionDossier.tsx:377-390 (parent link only); src/butlers/api/routers/sessions.py:97-148 (_build_where: no parent_session_id predicate); src/butlers/core/audit.py:23-88 (no session_id in the write path); src/butlers/api/routers/audit.py:304-330 (no session filter param)

findings.title: j/k selection contract half-implemented: no scroll-into-view/focus sync, and invalid ARIA on rows
findings.detail: SessionTable's selectedId prop docs promise the row 'carries data-session-id for the page's j/k roving focus to sync native DOM focus onto', but SessionsPage contains no code querying data-session-id, no scrollIntoView, no .focus() — j/k past the viewport edge moves selection (and swaps drawer content) invisibly. Also each interactive TableRow sets role='button' plus aria-selected; aria-selected is not a supported state for role=button (valid on gridcell/option/row/tab), so the selection state is announced inconsistently or not at all to AT.

audits.ideal: The ideal /sessions is the fleet's flight recorder and the trace spine's grand-central: it opens with a verdict that can never fabricate calm (every fan-out reports which butler DBs answered, and a missing source renders as a named degraded clause, never as zero failures), pins live and failed work above a chronological ledger whose every cell is provably sourced — cost and tokens including prompt-cache traffic, matching the Spend page to the cent. Selecting any row (mouse or j/k with the row scrolled into view) opens one canonical dossier — one detail endpoint, one cache key — that streams a running session's tool-call tail live from the daemon's capture buffer, freezes into the complete record on termination, and states retry lineage ('result from attempt 2 of 2') and owner corrections as first-class facts. Every identifier is a door in both directions: trace_id to the ingestion signal, request_id to sibling sessions, parent up AND children down, session to the audit actions it performed, cost to its purpose-tagged spend line — so any signal reaches root evidence in at most two keystrokes, and filters (enumerated trigger select, inclusive datetime ranges) always agree with the chart drawn beside them.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today the surface looks the part — verdict opener, KPI strip, pinned strip, URL filters, j/k shortcuts, a merged dossier — but its truthfulness has a hollow core: all four cross-butler reads use the silent fan_out, so a partial DB outage yields 'No sessions failed in the last 24h' and 404s existing sessions, the exact fabricated-calm failure the 07-04 epic purged from every other router; the drawer breaks on pinned rows and deep links because it still rides a redundant butler-scoped detail path; the 'streaming tail' poll watches a column the backend only writes at completion; cost and token figures exclude prompt-cache; retry/correction evidence is fetched and discarded; and the spine only walks upward — no children, no audit door, no way to promote the drawer to its permanent page. The instrument is assembled; what remains is making every number provable and every clause a two-way door.

findings.title: Notifications page KPI tiles and feed impersonate calm during a Switchboard outage (source_available plumbed but unread)
findings.detail: The degraded-envelope flags shipped for this endpoint are consumed ONLY by the verdict opener. NotificationStatsBar renders `stats?.total ?? 0`, `sent ?? 0`, `failed ?? 0` and a GREEN '0.0%' failure rate when the backend returns the all-zero degraded payload (notifications.py returns `_empty_notification_stats(source_available=False)` on pool failure). Worse, `NotificationListResponse.source_available` is never read by any non-test code: on outage the list endpoint 200s with an empty page + source_available=false and the page renders EmptyState 'No notifications found.' — a total delivery-plane outage is visually identical to a quiet, healthy feed, directly under a verdict opener that says otherwise. Also `failedCount` (drives the 'Acknowledge all failed' button) reads the same unguarded stats.

findings.title: One unscoped saved-views table cross-contaminates the fleet timeline and the ingestion ledger — foreign views apply as silent no-ops while highlighting active
findings.detail: `public.timeline_saved_views` has no surface/scope column and the list endpoint SELECTs every row. Both TimelinePage (/timeline) and the ingestion TimelineTab consume the same list via the same hook/query key. But their filter_spec vocabularies are disjoint: the fleet timeline writes/reads only {event_type, butler}; ingestion writes/reads {statuses, range, q, lanes...}. So a view saved on either surface appears as a chip on BOTH; clicking an ingestion-born chip (e.g. 'failed telegram hops') on /timeline sets ?view=<id>, clears filters, and renders the unfiltered firehose while the chip highlights as the active named view — the label lies about what is shown. Symmetrically in the other direction.

findings.title: Notification events on the fleet chronicle are spine-dead: no session/trace doors in the drawer, and the 'View in Notifications' link carries no predicate

audits.ideal: The ideal /timeline is the household's flight recorder: one keyboard-first chronicle where every clause is a door on the trace spine — j/k rove the rows, Enter peeks a drawer that shows the FULL message/prompt with session, trace, and notification-record doors one keystroke away, and every inbound link (Overview rows, verdict clauses) lands with its predicate so the drawer is already open. Time is navigable (jump-to-hour seeded from the ISO cursor the backend already accepts), the Errors lens covers every failure class including failed owner egress, saved views are scoped to the surface that authored them and fail loudly when unavailable, and the live head, badge, pill, and rollup all describe the same reality. The ideal /notifications is the delivery-plane ledger with the same honesty floor as its verdict opener: a Switchboard outage turns every tile and the feed itself into an explicit 'source unreachable' state — never zeros, never 'No notifications found' — each row deep-linkable by id, one triage verb with one name, and errors that offer retry instead of advice to refresh.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today both pages are structurally strong — URL-backed filters, live bus coverage, verdict opener, list triage on notifications, honest degraded banner and off-window ?event= resolution on timeline — but the honesty and spine work stopped one layer short of the pixels. The notifications page contradicts itself in a single viewport during an outage (verdict says unreachable, tiles say green 0.0%, feed says empty); the chronicle's notification clauses dead-end into a bare /notifications link because the read model never selects session_id/trace_id and the notifications page can't address a row by id; Overview drops the event predicate it already holds; the shared saved-views table lets each surface render the other's views as lying chips; and the flagship chronicle — the page most like a triage queue — is the one list surface with no j/k, no verbs, no time navigation, and a drawer capped at 120 characters. The gap is not missing primitives but unfinished adoption of the fleet's own conventions on its two most narrative surfaces.

audits.jarvis_gap: Today /issues and /audit-log are well-commented, URL-backed, and carry the shipped outcome trio + occurrences drill-down, but the pair still fails the two bars that matter most for a failure ledger: earned calm and an unbroken spine. The issues endpoint itself — the one surface whose whole job is surfacing failure — swallows its own data-source failures into a calm "No issues recorded" empty state with no degraded flag (the one fleet convention it was exempted from); acknowledging an unreachable butler silently un-acks itself on the next refetch; the occurrences drill-down re-derives groups unwindowed/uncapped (reintroducing the unbounded seq-scan bu-qvnce.13 killed, and 404ing when window and all-time group identity diverge); the issue→audit "View" door can land on a page whose default noise filter hides exactly the group's rows; and the ledger's Request ID dead-ends as plain text one click short of the session dossier. The audit page has no keyboard support, no free-text search (exact-match inputs firing a 1.17M-row count(*) per keystroke), and an Actor column that mixes butlers, path segments, and principals so "who did this" is unanswerable.

findings.title: /api/issues violates the fleet degraded-honesty convention — DB failure renders as calm 'No issues recorded'
findings.detail: The issues feed joins three sources (live reachability, audit-derived groups, ack store). Both DB-backed sources swallow every failure into a benign default: _list_audit_error_issues returns [] on db=None, missing pool, or ANY query exception; _list_dismissed_acks returns {} likewise. The response is ApiResponse[list[Issue]](data=issues) with no meta flag, and IssuesPanel renders the all-clear EmptyState. So a switchboard-pool outage makes the Issues page — the surface whose job is surfacing failure — show an empty, healthy feed. This endpoint was skipped by the bu-qvnce.1 DegradedSources sweep (that move covered butlers/memory/notifications/approvals/spend/settings/secrets). Failure-taxonomy shape 11, on the worst possible surface. Bonus: a failed acks query silently un-hides every acknowledged issue (noise instead of calm), equally unflagged.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/issues.py:104-126 (return [] on exception), :129-149 (return {} on exception), :329 (no meta flag); frontend/src/components/issues/IssuesPanel.tsx:204-222 (unconditional all-clear empty state); CLAUDE.md fleet-wide convention bu-qvnce.1

findings.title: Acknowledge on an unreachable-butler issue is a no-op that un-acks itself within seconds
findings.detail: Reachability issues get synthetic first_seen_at/last_seen_at = now() on EVERY feed fetch (issues.py:288-291). The ack watermark stores that instant (FE passes issue.last_seen_at); _still_acked compares the NEXT fetch's fresh now() against the watermark and finds it newer, so the ack lapses immediately. Worse, the dismiss mutation itself invalidates ["issues"] (use-issues.ts invalidateQueryKeys), triggering the refetch that resurrects the row — the owner clicks Acknowledge on the most critical issue type, the row disappears optimistically, then bounces back in ~1-2s. Shape 2 (success feedback for an effect that evaporates). The 'a' triage key and the palette 'Acknowledge issue' command hit the same path.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/issues.py:288-291 (synthetic now timestamps), :152-168 (_still_acked watermark compare); frontend/src/pages/IssuesPage.tsx:174-176, :202 (passes last_seen_at); frontend/src/hooks/use-issues.ts:79-84 (invalidate triggers refetch)

findings.title: Occurrences drill-down re-derives groups unwindowed and uncapped — unbounded scan is back, counts disagree, and group-identity drift 404s
findings.detail: list_issue_occurrences calls build_audit_group_query() with NO since and NO limit (issues.py:456), then a second full-CTE occurrences query — two parallel seq scans over public.audit_log (1.17M rows live, no index on result; verified EXPLAIN shows Parallel Seq Scan) on every row expand. This reintroduces exactly the unbounded all-time scan bu-qvnce.13 eliminated from the feed. Correctness: the feed row's issue_key was computed from the WINDOWED group (butlers list, schedule_names), but the lookup matches against ALL-TIME groups — when the butler set or schedule count differs across the boundary (e.g. 1 butler in 7d, 2 all-time → butler becomes 'multiple'; 1 schedule name → ':multiple' type slug), the keys diverge and the expand 404s with 'No active issue group found' for a row visibly on screen. Also the fetched occurrences and meta.total are all-time while the row says 'Seen 3x' in-window — the drill-down silently shows rows from months outside the selected window (live data spans 2026-03-27..07-10).
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/issues.py:456 (build_audit_group_query() bare), :474-486; src/butlers/api/models/__init__.py:247-284 (issue_key = type::butler, both window-dependent); audit_grouping.py:229-304 (butlers/schedule_names drive type+butler); live EXPLAIN: 'Parallel Seq Scan on audit_log Filter: (result = error)'; pg_indexes shows no result index

findings.title: Issue 'View' door lands on an audit view whose default noise filter hides the group's own rows (live: 34 heartbeat-error rows)
findings.detail: Issues grouping includes ALL result='error' rows (audit_grouping.py:112). The audit page defaults to kind=privileged, which excludes action NOT LIKE '%_heartbeat' — and since '_' is an unescaped LIKE single-char wildcard, 'POST /api/switchboard/heartbeat' (34 live error rows) matches and is excluded too. The View link built in issue_from_audit_group_row carries only result/actor/action params — never noise=all and never the group's error_summary predicate — so clicking View on a heartbeat-error group lands on a privileged-filtered list showing OTHER switchboard errors (or an empty state), not the group's rows. The door on the trace spine opens onto the wrong room. Secondary: because the link never carries the group key, even for ordinary groups it shows every error row for that actor, not the group — the occurrences panel mitigates in-page but the /audit-log hop stays lossy; and the 'privileged only' label itself overpromises: 'session' (13,852) and 'llm_api_call' (9,237) routine rows pass the filter, so the default view is mostly operational noise anyway.

findings.title: Audit pagination survives pivot-link navigation — past-the-end pages render a lying 'No audit entries found'
findings.detail: page is component useState, reset only inside handleFilterChange/handleClearFilters. Clicking an actor/action pivot cell (Link to /audit-log?actor=X) or arriving via a ?key=/?result= deep link while page>0 keeps the stale page: if the new filter has fewer pages, entries=[] with total>0, so the table shows the EmptyState claiming no entries exist while the footer reads 'Page 6 of 1'. Filters are URL-backed (bu-qvnce.13) but pagination is not, so the URL is not actually the sole source of truth for what's displayed.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/AuditLogPage.tsx:53 (useState page), :107-121 (reset only in handleFilterChange); AuditLogTable.tsx:162-170 (EmptyState on entries.length===0); AuditLogPage.tsx:297-321 (pagination renders when total>0)

findings.title: Actor column mixes three vocabularies — the ledger cannot answer 'who did this'
findings.detail: public.audit_log.actor holds (a) butler daemon names ('switchboard', 'education'), (b) path segments inferred by _infer_butler for dashboard mutations ('approvals', 'settings', 'ingestion', 'secrets', 'dashboard:rest-api'), and (c) the principal 'owner' from other writers — 23 distinct actors live. An owner-initiated PATCH via the dashboard is recorded with actor=<path segment> while the true principal is buried in metadata.user_context ('owner'). The ledger of record thus can't distinguish owner actions from autonomous butler actions — the single most important axis for an audit trail in a sovereign one-person system (shape 10: real data under a mislabeled axis).
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/dashboard_audit_middleware.py:70-88 (_infer_butler path inference → actor); audit_emit.py:33-36 (_OWNER_PRINCIPAL only lands in user_context); live query: actors include switchboard(1.16M), approvals(1106), owner(929), dashboard:rest-api(118), settings(125)

findings.title: Filtered-empty impersonates true-empty on Issues — the audit→issues ?q= door silently fails for errors older than the 7d default window
findings.detail: IssuesPanel's EmptyState has no awareness of active q/severity/butler filters or the window: zero matches renders 'No issues recorded. Issues appear when butlers report errors or warnings.' The 'View in Issues →' link from an audit error row (?q=first-error-line) searches only the client-loaded default-7d feed, so for any error >7d old (or a currently-acked group) the hop lands on that lying all-clear — the owner is told the issue doesn't exist when it's one window-pill away.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/issues/IssuesPanel.tsx:204-222 (filter-blind empty state); frontend/src/pages/IssuesPage.tsx:96-116 (q filters the windowed feed client-side); AuditLogTable.tsx:334-342 (View in Issues link, no window param)

findings.title: Audit filter inputs: exact-match semantics, one seq-scan count(*) per keystroke, no free-text search, no until bound
findings.detail: Actor/action inputs write the URL per keystroke (replace:true), each firing a fresh query pair including SELECT count(*) over 1.17M rows (parallel seq scan; the NOT LIKE privileged predicate defeats indexes). Backend matching is exact (actor = $, action = $), so typing 'swi' shows an empty table until the full value is entered — a search-shaped input with lookup semantics. The ledger has no substring search over action/note/error/metadata, no ?until upper bound, and no way to discover the action vocabulary (owner must guess exact strings like 'model.priority').
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/AuditLogPage.tsx:107-121 (per-keystroke setSearchParams → new query key); src/butlers/api/routers/audit.py:381-407 (exact-match conditions, count_sql), :308 (since only, no until); live EXPLAIN count(*) WHERE result='error' → Parallel Seq Scan; docs/operations/data-retention.md:63-67 (count budget note)

findings.title: Issues page load is gated on live MCP pings to the whole fleet — slowest exactly during an incident
findings.detail: Every GET /api/issues runs _check_butler_reachability against every configured butler with 5s get_client + 5s ping timeouts (retry on stale connection): a down butler stalls the feed ~10s before first paint — the five-second verification bar is broken precisely when the owner opens the page because something is wrong. Nothing caches or reuses the heartbeat/status data the system already maintains; the same full-fleet ping storm re-fires on every 5-min reconcile and every bus-driven invalidation (i.e. after every error row, including the owner's own ack mutations).
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/issues.py:45 (_STATUS_TIMEOUT_S=5.0), :190-227 (two awaits × 5s, retry loop), :275-280 (per-request fan-out, no cache); use-issues.ts:38-42 (bus invalidation + 5-min reconcile re-trigger it)

audits.ideal: The ideal /issues + /audit-log pair is one continuous failure instrument on the trace spine: the Issues feed is the fleet's triage inbox — degraded-honest (any source outage is named inline, never rendered as calm), instant (reachability served from the heartbeat store the daemons already maintain, not a 10-second ping storm), with acks that mean what they say for every issue type (an unreachable-butler ack holds until recovery, an error-group ack holds until true recurrence) — and every group is a door: expand for its exact windowed occurrences with honest 'showing N of M', one keypress to the session dossier behind any occurrence, one keypress to the ledger filtered to precisely that group's rows with the noise default automatically widened. The Audit Log is the ledger of record: append-only, principal-honest (who = owner|butler|connector, where = subsystem, both first-class columns), searchable by debounced substring across action/error/note with a discoverable action vocabulary and a bounded time range, keyboard-walkable with j/k and Enter-to-expand, live via the same bus event that feeds Issues, and every Request ID a two-way door between ledger row and session dossier. Nothing the pair renders — an empty state, a count, a page number — is ever something the system cannot prove.

audits.ideal: The ideal /approvals is the household's autonomy contract made legible: a queue ranked by the system's own risk classification (not a client-side regex), where every pending dossier explains itself and every DECIDED dossier is a complete decision record — who decided (you, a named standing rule, or system expiry), when, the deny reason you typed, and what actually happened when it ran (execution_result), each clause a door to the originating session, the audit entry, and the governing rule. The autonomy panel is a real ledger, not a list: a rule's "14 uses" opens the 14 actions it fired, so trust is auditable in two keystrokes. Expiry is a real contract — expired actions are swept and cannot fire — and countdowns tick live. Partial backend outages are named inline (a butler's approvals pool being down never renders as a calm, shorter queue), and every decision path (button, keyboard, palette, dashboard row) shares one undo-window contract.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today the pending-side loop is genuinely strong (ranked rail, keyboard triage with undo windows, honest dispatch toasts, verdict opener), but the surface goes dark the moment a decision is made: the decided dossier shows only a status word — decided_by/decided_at exist in the payload and are never rendered, the deny reason is string-smuggled into decided_by and invisible everywhere, and execution_result/approval_rule_id are dropped by the backend detail builder — so the trace spine ends at the decision instead of at root evidence. The autonomy ledger shows counts with no doors (no rule→actions path, no human-vs-rule distinction in history), expiry is advisory theater (no sweep is scheduled, approve has no expiry guard, countdowns never tick), and the degraded-honesty flags the backend already emits (meta.sources_degraded) are consumed nowhere on the page, so a butler-pool outage renders as a calm queue — the exact failure-impersonates-health sin the fleet convention exists to prevent.

findings.title: Decided dossier omits the entire decision record (decided_by/decided_at/deny reason/execution_result/rule) and a code comment falsely claims otherwise
findings.evidence: frontend/src/api/types.ts:2833-2834 (ApprovalDetail carries decided_by/decided_at) but the Dossier body (frontend/src/pages/ApprovalsPage.tsx:621-791) renders neither; ApprovalsPage.tsx:1064-1067 comment claims 'decided_by/decided_at shown' — false. Backend _pending_action_to_detail (src/butlers/api/routers/approvals.py:288-303) drops execution_result and approval_rule_id even though the row and ApprovalAction carry them (src/butlers/modules/approvals/models.py:104-105, approvals.py:267-268). Deny reason is smuggled into the decided_by string — operations.py:273-276 `decided_by = f"{decided_by} (reason: {escaped_reason})"` — so the 'Deny reason (optional)' input (ApprovalsPage.tsx:527-541) writes text no console surface can ever show back (console-side decorative persistence, taxonomy shape 1).
findings.detail: History rows link to /approvals/:id 'read-only dossiers' that cannot answer: who decided this, when, why was it denied, did it succeed when it ran, and which rule auto-approved it. This is the prompt's decided-dossier-completeness focus and is NOT covered by bu-24lu6.2 (which adds blast_radius/reversibility/typed-evidence at the gate, not the post-decision record).

findings.title: meta.sources_degraded from /api/approvals and /history is consumed nowhere on the page — a butler pool outage renders as a calm, shorter queue and can still show the all-clear verdict
findings.evidence: Backend sets it: src/butlers/api/routers/approvals.py:1561 and :1624 (DegradedSources → ApiMeta.sources_degraded). FE consumption: `grep -rn sources_degraded frontend/src/` hits only secrets files (use-secrets-inventory.ts, SecretsPage.test.tsx) — zero hits in ApprovalsPage/approvals components. ApprovalsVerdictOpener passes only isLoading/isError per whole query (approvals-verdict-opener.tsx:93-96); DispatchVerdict has no partial-degradation input (dispatch-verdict.tsx:30-35).
findings.detail: Violates the fleet-wide convention in butlers/CLAUDE.md ('gate any verdict/all-clear renderer on the relevant flag(s)… never suppress it') and failure-taxonomy shape 11 on the exact surface where a missed approval is most consequential. One failing pool out of N drops that butler's pending approvals silently; 'No approvals waiting.' can render while approvals exist.

findings.title: Approval expiry is advisory theater: no scheduled sweep, no approve-time guard, orphaned FE sweep hook, and countdown chips never tick
findings.evidence: expire sweep exists only as manual MCP tool/REST endpoint: src/butlers/modules/approvals/module.py:935 (_expire_stale_actions), approvals.py:1043; `grep -rn expire_stale src/butlers/core/ src/butlers/jobs/ roster/` = zero hits (nothing schedules it). approve_action validates only status, never expires_at (src/butlers/modules/approvals/operations.py:79-105). useExpireStaleActions has 0 non-test callers (grep count). FE countdowns computed at render with Date.now(), no interval timer (only useEffect is focus-sync, ApprovalsPage.tsx:1344); reconcile poll is 5 min (poll-policy.ts:23).
findings.detail: A 'pending' action whose window elapsed days ago is still approvable and dispatchable (a high-blast outbound send included), and because expiryUrgency ranks past-expiry as 4 (ApprovalsPage.tsx:177) a dead item permanently squats the top rail slot. Meanwhile 'expires in 12m' can read 12m until the item is gone.

findings.title: Autonomy ledger has no doors: use counts are dead-ends, rule-approved and human-approved actions are indistinguishable, and no endpoint can list a rule's actions
findings.evidence: autonomy-panel.tsx:90-93 renders use_count as plain text with no link; pending_actions.approval_rule_id exists (models.py:105) and auto-approval writes decided_by=f"rule:{rule_id}" (gate.py:661), but ApprovalActionParams has no rule_id filter (frontend/src/api/types.ts:2900-2906) and no router route filters by it (approvals.py:455-564). History rows render only status/tool/butler (ApprovalsPage.tsx:1051-1087) — decided_by never surfaced anywhere, so 'a rule did this' vs 'I did this' vs 'system:expiry' is invisible.
findings.detail: The panel's stated purpose is 'What the fleet may do unsupervised', but the owner cannot audit what a grant actually DID — the trace spine from grant → uses → outcomes has zero doors. (The 'always ask' baseline endpoint is already tracked in bu-uimqo and excluded here; this is the separate rule→actions/decided-by axis.)

findings.title: Approve-with-edits is backend-complete and client-complete but has zero UI
findings.evidence: POST /{id}/approve accepts edits and applies them transactionally (src/butlers/api/routers/approvals.py:2072-2110); approveApproval(actionId, request?) already takes ApprovalApproveRequest (frontend/src/api/client.ts:3557-3568); ApprovalsPage calls approveMut.mutate(id) with no edits path anywhere (ApprovalsPage.tsx:1470, use-approval-decisions.ts:144).
findings.detail: Failure-taxonomy shape 5. The natural JARVIS gesture — fix the message text, then approve — forces a deny+re-propose round-trip today. Not covered by bu-24lu6 (telegram one-tap/decision memory) or bu-uimqo.

findings.title: Command-palette 'Approve next' bypasses the undo-window contract its displayed 'a' binding promises
findings.evidence: ApprovalsPage.tsx:1365-1376: perform() calls approveMut.mutate(effectiveSelected) directly and advertises binding ["a"], while the actual 'a' key routes through scheduleDecision with a 5s undo window (ApprovalsPage.tsx:1307-1312, use-approval-decisions.ts:44,196-213).
findings.detail: Same verb, same displayed key, two irreversibility contracts — the palette path fires instantly with no undo toast. Violates design-bar bias 5 (one control, one meaning) on the page's most consequential action.

findings.title: Stalled (approved-never-ran) actions become unreachable once 30 newer decisions exist
findings.evidence: Both the History section and the verdict's stalled clause scan only getApprovalsHistory(undefined, 30) (ApprovalsPage.tsx:1026,1190; approvals-verdict-opener.tsx:54-67). No console surface queries status='approved' directly (flat endpoint state=decided exists, approvals.py:1526-1527, but is uncalled: grep getApprovalsFlat shows only 'waiting' callers). Retry is only offered on visible history rows (ApprovalsPage.tsx:1077-1079).
findings.detail: A dispatch failure older than the 30-decision window silently exits every ledger and its retry affordance — failure vanishing by pagination on the one status that represents an un-run promised action.

findings.title: Detail lookup folds transient pool errors into 404, and the FE dossier error state is a dead end
findings.evidence: approvals.py:2046-2062: per-pool `except Exception: continue` then unconditional 404 'Approval not found' — a transient failure of the owning butler's pool reports the approval as nonexistent. FE renders a bare 'failed to load dossier' with no retry, no 404-vs-outage distinction, bypassing QueryBoundary (ApprovalsPage.tsx:444-450).
findings.detail: A push-notification deep link (/approvals/:id) hitting a transient pool blip tells the owner the decision doesn't exist. Same _find_action_pool pattern at approvals.py:244-245 affects approve/deny/defer 404s.

audits.jarvis_gap: Today the calendar is feature-rich (drag/resize, quick-add, find-time, proposals, duplicates, radar, prep rail, portability) but its truth plumbing is wired to only the primary query: every secondary source (meta, accounts, overlays, day-briefing, conflicts scan, search) degrades to a calm empty on HTTP error — one literally prints "Tomorrow is clear" when the fetch failed — and the per-source sync freshness the workspace read already returns is never rendered on the canvas, so a days-stale or auth-broken source looks like a healthy week. Interactionally, an event can only be rescheduled by dragging inside the currently visible week/day grid (the edit dialog's update mode is dead code), concurrent events fully occlude each other, there is no now-line, no deep-link into a specific event, and three concrete timezone label/compute mismatches ship in the click-create, masthead, and recurrence-preview paths.

findings.title: Every secondary data source fails to benign-empty; day briefing fabricates 'Tomorrow is clear' on fetch error
findings.detail: The page joins ~8 queries but only workspaceQuery has an error surface (CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:4621-4632). All others render calm empties on HTTP error: (a) metaQuery.isError is never read — connected_sources/writable_calendars default to [] (2131-2146), so a meta outage renders 'No connected sources.' in the Sources dialog (5582-5585), disables Create/quick-add, and presents as 'you have no calendars'; (b) accountsQuery error → accounts section silently absent (5518-5521); (c) search palette has no isError branch — an HTTP error falls through searchAvailable=(undefined!==false)=true → results=[] → renders 'No matching events.' (1977-1981, 2052-2055); (d) dayBriefingQuery.isError is never passed — DayBriefingCard receives groups=[]/hasDomainContext=false and renders 'No domain context for this day. Tomorrow is clear.' (DayBriefingCard.tsx:147-151, wired at CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:4532-4539) — a literal all-clear on a failed request; (e) conflictsQuery error → conflictsAvailable=false → banner renders nothing (2320-2325); (f) overlaysQuery error → toggle shows '· none' (4444-4446). This is failure-taxonomy shape 11 and violates the fleet degraded-envelope convention (butlers/CLAUDE.md 'a source that raises... must never render as a truthful empty/zero/all-clear result'). bu-5rmhbo shipped server-side available:false envelopes; plain client-side fetch errors were never covered.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:2131-2146,5582-5585,1977-1981,2052-2055,2320-2325,4444-4446,4532-4539; frontend/src/components/calendar/DayBriefingCard.tsx:147-151; grep 'metaQuery\.' shows zero isError reads

findings.title: Sync freshness/errors invisible on the canvas — a broken or stale source renders as a healthy grid
findings.detail: The workspace read returns per-source source_freshness (sync_state, staleness_ms, last_error, error_kind, full_sync_required — api/types.ts:776-805, response field at 827) but the page NEVER reads it (grep 'source_freshness' in CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx: zero hits; the page renders freshness only from the meta endpoint's connectedSources, and only INSIDE the Sources dialog at 5765-5791). If Google sync broke 3 days ago (token_expired), the grid shows old events with zero indication; the owner must open the Sources dialog to discover it. The timeline surface earned a stale strip in the 07-04 epic; the calendar — the surface where staleness means missed meetings — has none. Compounding it, the ConflictRadarBanner's documented degraded mode is to 'render nothing at all (silent)' (ConflictRadarBanner.tsx:11-14, 164), which is indistinguishable from a clean week — absence of the banner IS an all-clear signal, exactly what SourceDegradedNote vocabulary forbids suppressing.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/api/types.ts:776-805,827; frontend/src/pages/CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:5765-5791 (dialog-only rendering); frontend/src/components/calendar/ConflictRadarBanner.tsx:11-14,164

findings.title: No precision-reschedule path: the user-event edit dialog's update mode is dead code, and drag is the only way to change times
findings.detail: userEventDialogMode is only ever set to 'create' (single setter call at 2915) and activeUserEntry is only ever set to null (2916, 3441, 5813), so the dialog's entire edit branch — 'Edit user event' title (5823), 'Update event' submit (6085), the action==='update' payload path in submitUserEventForm (3508-3514), and fallbackOwner resolution (3472-3478) — is unreachable. The detail panel edits title/description/location on blur but renders 'When' read-only (1768-1778) with no time inputs. Net effect: the only way to change an event's start/end is a pointer drag inside the currently visible week/day grid; moving an event to next month, or rescheduling from the month/agenda views, is impossible in the UI. Dead cruft + missing core affordance in one.

findings.title: Concurrent events fully occlude each other on the week/day grid
findings.detail: Timed entries render as absolutely positioned blocks spanning the full column width (className 'absolute inset-x-0.5 z-10 ...' with top/height from start/duration, 5226-5240). There is no overlap-cluster layout (no column-splitting/width-sharing code exists — grep for cluster/columnize returns nothing), so two events at the same time stack exactly on top of each other: the one rendered later hides the earlier one entirely, which becomes invisible AND unclickable. The only hint is the amber left edge from the conflict radar (5228-5230) — which exists only on week/day views and goes silent whenever the scan is degraded or errored (finding 2). For an operator console whose job is conflict awareness, the conflicting events themselves are the thing the grid cannot display.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:5226-5240 (full-width absolute blocks); grep 'cluster|overlapColumn|layoutEvents|columnize' → no layout function; ConflictRadarBanner degraded-silent at ConflictRadarBanner.tsx:164

findings.title: Three concrete timezone truth defects shipped: masthead label, click-to-create instant, recurrence-preview caption
findings.detail: Beyond the known one-timezone-sweep idea, three specific mismatches are live: (a) the masthead eyebrow displays the BROWSER timezone ('Calendar · ... · {timezone}' at 4207, from Intl at 2128) while the grid buckets and renders in the WORKSPACE defaultTimezone (2745, 5203) — the page label lies about the axis the grid is drawn in (shape 10); (b) single-click-to-create computes the instant browser-locally ('new Date(day); clickedDate.setHours(...)' 5085-5092) while drag-create resolves the same grid minutes via isoAtMinuteInTz(day, min, defaultTimezone) (3204-3208) — clicking a 14:00 slot prefills the wrong hour whenever browser tz ≠ workspace tz; (c) the recurrence preview's caption claims 'Preview ({browser tz})' (6394) but formats every occurrence in defaultTimezone (6411-6415). Also the workspace query sends browser timezone as its timezone param (2300) while the window bounds are computed in workspace tz (2156-2158).
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:2128,4207 vs 2745,5203 (label); 5085-5092 vs 3204-3208 (click vs drag); 6394 vs 6411-6415 (preview caption); 2300 vs 2156-2158 (query param)

findings.title: No now-line or current-time marker in the time grid
findings.detail: The week/day grid scrolls to a static DEFAULT_SCROLL_HOUR=7.5 on mount (531, 2669-2673) and renders no current-time indicator of any kind (grep for now-line/current-time logic returns nothing; 'today' exists only as a header/date-cell highlight at 4931, 4815). The single most-used orientation cue of any calendar — where is now, what's next — is absent, so five-second orientation ('am I late for something?') requires reading hour labels and mentally locating the current time.

findings.title: No inbound doors: nothing outside the sidebar links into /calendar, and no event is deep-linkable
findings.detail: The only inbound reference to /calendar in the app is nav-config.ts:89. URL state covers view/range/anchor/filters/overlays but NOT the selected entry (selectedEntry is plain component state, 2527-2528), so a specific event cannot be linked, shared, or landed on: a notification about a butler-created event, a session dossier, or even the calendar's own Activity audit rows (which link OUT to /sessions/{id} at 1450-1456) cannot open the event they concern on the grid. The search palette's jump-and-flash machinery (handleSearchJump + flashedEntryId, 2681-2724) already implements exactly the landing behavior a ?entry= param needs — it's just not URL-addressable. This is the move-13 'predicate-carrying inbound doors' pattern unapplied to this surface.

audits.ideal: The JARVIS-grade calendar is the household's single time surface and it never lies about time: the masthead carries one timezone (the workspace's), a red now-line anchors the grid to the present, and a quiet freshness plaque derived from the workspace read's own source_freshness says 'all sources current · 2m ago' or names the broken one with a Reconnect door — while every secondary join (briefing, radar, overlays, search, accounts) that fails says so inline in SourceDegradedNote vocabulary instead of impersonating a clear day. Every event is a door and a destination: concurrent events split side-by-side so conflicts are visible in the geometry itself, any event is addressable by URL so notifications, session dossiers, and audit rows land directly on it with a flash, and its detail panel offers precise datetime editing (with the recurrence scope sheet) so rescheduling to any week is two keystrokes, not a drag constrained to the visible window. Quick-add corrections happen in human time pickers, the whole surface participates in the prefetch/poll/event-bus spine so it opens instantly and updates on push, and the implementation lives in composable components under components/calendar/ with zero dead modes.
