audits.jarvis_gap: Today the health cluster is honest CRUD with an editorial landing page: seven pages, QueryBoundary on the six tracker lists, a templated briefing, and a working measurement chart. But the connective tissue the vision demands is missing or broken: every real proactive insight lands on the wrong page (the FE category switch matches zero categories the insight jobs actually emit), the adherence engine fabricates red alarms for new and PRN medications, the leading trend/chart surfaces render fetch failures as serene emptiness, blood-pressure trend is structurally unreachable, and the owner's sleep/steps/HRV live only on an ops tab under old Card chrome while the domain surface shows four hardcoded vitals with no units, no age, no deltas, and no doors. The manifesto's core promises — patterns emerging over time, trajectory, the doctor-visit answer — exist only as backend insight jobs whose output the UI cannot route; nothing on the surface renders a pattern, a reference range, or provenance. The gap to JARVIS is not more data; it is honest denominators, working doors, and rendering the intelligence the backend already computes.

findings.title: Insight doors route on a category vocabulary the backend never emits — every health insight lands on /health/measurements
findings.detail: insightHref() switches on categories 'medication', 'adherence', 'measurement', 'blood_pressure', 'heart_rate', 'weight', 'blood_sugar', 'symptom', 'condition', 'meal', 'nutrition'. The insight-scan jobs that populate public.insight_candidates for butler=health emit 'measurement-gap', 'medication-refill', 'symptom-trend', 'health-streak', 'correlation-adherence', 'correlation-drift', 'correlation-environment' — none match, and the jobs write no metadata.href. Every FE branch is dead code and every real insight falls through to default '/health/measurements': a medication-refill alert links to the measurements page, a symptom-trend to measurements. Failure-taxonomy shape 12 (backend-narrow vs frontend-wide vocabulary) on the hottest signal->evidence path of the surface.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/HealthOverviewPage.tsx:192-212 (switch cases) vs roster/health/jobs/health_jobs.py:288,400,462,523,691,774,886 (category= values); grep for 'href' in health_jobs.py returns nothing

findings.title: Adherence denominator fabricates a red alarm for newly-added and PRN medications
findings.detail: GET /medications/{id}/adherence computes expected_doses = round(doses_per_day * window) with window defaulting to 30 days and effective_start = end - 30d, never clamped to the medication's created_at. A daily med added 3 days ago with perfect adherence shows expected=30, taken=3 -> 10% -> StateDot 'error' (red) and red text. 'as needed'/'prn' map to 1.0 dose/day ('fallback: assume once daily'), so a PRN med taken twice a month is permanently ~7% red. The system renders alarm the data cannot support — the inverse of fabricated calm, equally corrosive to earned trust.
findings.evidence: roster/health/api/router.py:608-656 (window computation, expected = round(doses_per_day * window)); roster/health/tools/_medication_utils.py:34-35 ('as needed': 1.0); frontend/src/components/health/MedicationTracker.tsx:105-113 (rate<50 -> 'error' dot), 140-146 (red text <50)

findings.title: Blood-pressure trend is structurally empty — 'No trend' rendered as truth above a populated BP chart
findings.detail: The trend SQL only aggregates rows where jsonb_typeof(metadata->'value') IN ('number','string') and the value matches a numeric regex. Blood pressure is stored as a compound object {systolic, diastolic} (MeasurementForm.buildValue), so trend buckets for blood_pressure are always []. MeasurementChart offers blood_pressure as a first-class tab and renders 'No trend for blood pressure in the last Nd' forever, directly above a raw chart full of BP readings. Shape 9: the control implies an axis the system never populates.
findings.evidence: roster/health/api/router.py:1800-1812 (jsonb_typeof filter + numeric regex); frontend/src/components/health/MeasurementForm.tsx:114-119 (compound {systolic,diastolic}); frontend/src/components/health/MeasurementChart.tsx:33-41 (blood_pressure in CHART_TYPES), 259-260 (empty-state line, no data ever)

findings.title: Fetch failure impersonates empty on the chart, trend, nutrition totals, and adherence statements
findings.detail: Four sibling read-paths skipped the QueryBoundary the trackers adopted: (1) MeasurementChart trend section has no isError branch — a failed trend fetch renders 'No trend for X in the last Nd'; (2) the raw chart has no isError branch — a failed measurements fetch renders 'No X readings for this range'; (3) MealsPage DailyTotals computes noData = !isLoading && (!data || meal_count===0), so an error renders 'No nutrition data for this window'; (4) MedicationTracker AdherenceStatement renders 'No doses logged yet' when the adherence query errors. All four are new instances of error-as-empty (shape 8/11) on this surface after the fleet-wide truth amnesty.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/health/MeasurementChart.tsx:253-260 and 343-346 (isLoading/empty only, no isError); frontend/src/pages/MealsPage.tsx:71-73,117-121; frontend/src/components/health/MedicationTracker.tsx:121-133

audits.ideal: The JARVIS health pane opens on the owner's current physiological state: fresh vitals with units, reading age, and trend deltas (sleep last night beside weight and BP), each KPI cell a door into a pre-filtered trajectory view where the chart, trend list, and reading log all obey one URL predicate and draw the owner's own reference ranges; the attention index routes every insight — refill due, symptom recurrence, drift, environment correlation — to the exact filtered evidence that produced it, one keystroke away; adherence is stated with an honest denominator (windows clamped to the medication's life, PRN meds exempt from rates); patterns the manifesto promises are rendered surfaces, not buried LLM text — per-symptom recurrence histograms, drift annotations, correlation panels; every reading carries provenance (owner, Google Health, butler session) with a trace door to the writing session; failure is always named (a dead trend source reads 'trend unavailable', never 'no trend'); and a single palette verb composes the doctor-visit dossier for any date range so the continuity promise — 'your doctor asks, the butler has the answer' — is one action, not an archaeology project.

audits.jarvis_gap: Today /spend is the best-composed analytics page in the fleet (verdict opener, honest movers, evidence tables, rules co-located with signals) but its posture layer — the one question the page exists to answer — can fabricate calm: the forecast endpoint has no degraded envelope at all, the MTD it displays is priced from a different data source than the MTD the spawn-deny gate enforces, a ceiling breach that halts the entire fleet renders as nothing more than a budget graph at 100%, and two controls (per-rule "Saved 7d", per-call cap) show real numbers under captions that describe a different computation than the one that ran. The ideal is a budget authority the owner can trust in five seconds: one ledger-derived MTD that is literally the enforced number; the ceiling presented as the fleet-halting breaker it is, with a live "N dispatches denied" state and doors from each denial to its dispatch attempt; every schedule/session/mover row carrying a one-keystroke "cap this" verb that pre-fills a rule scoped to that exact evidence; and every rule showing its true effect (matched/denied counts, last-matched, honestly-attributed savings) so the notice-spike-to-cap-cause loop the page's own header promises actually closes on this surface.

findings.title: Forecast/posture layer has no degraded envelope — butler outage renders as lower spend and a vanished ceiling
findings.detail: The page's primary layer (verdict opener, KPI strip, over-ceiling alert, forecast chart) is fed by GET /api/spend/forecast, which is the ONE spend fan-out endpoint with no unavailable_butlers tracking: the MCP fallback is invoked without a tracker, ForecastResponse has no degraded field, and the ceiling read swallows all DB errors with `except Exception: pass` — so a failed ceiling read renders as ceiling '—', the red over-ceiling alert silently disappears, and CeilingEdit shows 'Set ceiling' as if none was ever configured. An unreachable butler's month of spend is silently subtracted from MTD/projection. Violates the fleet-wide bu-qvnce.1 honest-aggregation convention on the exact surface move 1 shipped for. Failure-taxonomy shape 11.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/spend.py:1265-1267 (fallback `_get_butler_daily_stats(...)` — no tracker= param), :1219-1226 (ForecastResponse: no unavailable/degraded field), :1303-1312 (`except Exception: pass` on ceiling read); frontend/src/pages/SpendPage.tsx:1398-1412 (SpendVerdictOpener fed only forecastError boolean), :1444-1446 (KpiStrip renders confident numbers)

findings.title: Two MTD truths: the displayed budget number is not the enforced budget number
findings.detail: The page's MTD/ceiling-% is priced from per-butler `sessions` tables via fan-out (sessions_daily + pricing), while the spawner's ceiling DENY gate prices `public.token_usage_ledger` (check_monthly_ceiling / _MTD_USAGE_BY_MODEL_SQL). Different sources, independently computed (settings_console computes yet a third MTD). When they diverge the dashboard can show 92% used while spawns are already being denied, or show over-ceiling while the gate still allows. The number that actually governs the fleet is never displayed anywhere.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/spend.py:1251-1283 (forecast MTD from per-butler sessions fan-out) vs src/butlers/core/model_routing.py:1078-1141 (check_monthly_ceiling prices token_usage_ledger, _MTD_USAGE_BY_MODEL_SQL at :444-456); src/butlers/api/routers/settings_console.py:180-220 (third independent MTD)

findings.title: Ceiling breach halts the fleet, and /spend shows nothing about it — denials are queryable but unwired
findings.detail: At MTD >= ceiling the spawner DENIES every spawn (outcome='quota_skip'); same for per-call-cap denials. The page's only red state is 'Projected EOM exceeds ceiling' — a projection message. There is no 'spawns are being denied NOW' state, no denial count, and no door to the denial evidence. Backend GET /api/dispatch/attempts already exposes quota_skip rows; zero frontend consumers exist (shape 5, backend-ready/frontend-not-wired). The single most consequential thing the spend system can do — stop the household staff — is invisible on the spend surface.

findings.title: 'Saved 7d' mislabels fleet-wide model usage as per-rule savings (shape 10)

Two rules routing to the same model each claim the identical 'savings' (double count); usage that would have hit the model anyway (e.g. via catalog tier resolution) is credited to the rule; a rule routing to a reasoning model shows a large negative number it did not cause. The rules table renders this as a per-rule 'Saved 7d' column — a true number under a false caption.

findings.title: Per-call cap overpromises: input-side-only estimate, fail-open without a token budget (shape 2)

DENY gate'. Actual enforcement: a pre-spawn worst-case estimate of INPUT cost only (output tokens explicitly excluded), and when the dispatch has no max_token_budget the cap is skipped entirely with an info log. A call can pass a $0.50 cap at $0.30 estimated input and spend unbounded output dollars; unbudgeted dispatches bypass the cap silently. No surface reports unenforceable-cap allowances or post-hoc breaches.

findings.title: Fading lifecycle is a dead data contract: sweep writes metadata.status, entire UI reads validity='fading' which nothing ever writes
findings.detail: The just-shipped decay sweep marks fading facts via metadata['status']='fading' (and clears it on recovery), but the dashboard's entire fading axis keys on the validity column: stats count `WHERE validity='fading'`, the facts list filter, the register 'fading' pill, the attention-rail 'important facts fading' condition (useFacts({validity:'fading',importance_min:8})), the pipeline band 'fading N' numeral, and the row/detail dimming (`fact.validity==='fading'`, documented as 'the single affordance for decay'). grep across src/ shows NO writer of validity='fading' anywhere. Result: fading count is structurally 0 forever, the fading pill always returns 'No facts answer this.', attention condition 4 can never fire, dimming is unreachable. The FE comment 'the server owns the fading threshold' is true — but the server publishes it to a key the API never reads. MCP-side retrieval (management.py:95-101) consistently uses metadata->>'status', so the runtime and the dashboard speak two different lifecycle vocabularies over the same table.

findings.title: Memory surface never consumes its own degraded envelope; every failure renders as calm emptiness
findings.detail: The backend memory router emits meta.pools_failed via the qvnce.1 DegradedSources tracker, but grep finds zero frontend consumers of pools_failed — and no memory component adopted SourceDegradedNote (adopters: secrets, spend, sessions, topology, etc.). Worse, no memory component has any isError branch on queries (only the two mutation error lines in HousekeepingBand): a stats fetch failure leaves the Overture blank forever (reserved min-heights, indistinguishable from loading) and renders the AttentionRail as 'Nothing waiting.' + 'Nothing observed yet.'; a facts/episodes fetch failure renders 'The ledger is empty.' / 'Nothing observed yet.'; SearchResults renders 'Nothing in the books.' both during pending (a flash on every submit — no placeholderData floor) and permanently on error. Additionally isWriteupOverdue returns false when last_consolidation_at is null, so a consolidation pipeline that has NEVER run also shows 'Nothing waiting.' This is the exact failure-impersonates-health shape the fleet convention (CLAUDE.md bu-qvnce.1) forbids, on the surface whose backend flag shipped in the same epic.

Overpromise (taxonomy shape 2/10) on a commit-class control.

findings.title: Confirm on an expired/retracted fact promises re-inking that cannot happen; retract is unrecoverable
findings.detail: The CommitFooter always renders Confirm ('Re-inks the fact: resets decay from today') and Retract on every fact regardless of validity. confirm_memory only sets last_confirmed_at=now() — it never restores validity to 'active' nor clears metadata.status. The decay sweep only scans WHERE validity='active', so an expired fact confirmed by the owner stays expired forever: the mutation succeeds, the UI refetches, and nothing changes — agents still won't retrieve it. Retract has no inverse anywhere (no un-retract/restore endpoint), so a mis-retract is permanent while the adjacent Confirm pill implies recoverability. Violates design-bar recovery ('never replace a confirm with an undo that can't undo') and the earned-calm bar (success feedback for a no-op).

audits.ideal: The ideal /memory is the household's belief audit: the Overture answers "is remembering working" with numbers the runtime actually lives by — one lifecycle vocabulary shared by sweep, retrieval, API, and ink, so a fading fact dims, an expired rule leaves the rulebook count, and the pipeline band's numerals are provably the same ones agents retrieve against. Every red or amber row in the attention rail is a door onto root evidence and a lever: a dead-lettered episode shows its last_consolidation_error and attempts and offers requeue; an anti-pattern rule offers retire; a stale-embedding row offers a fleet-wide re-embed that actually clears the count it cites. Failure never impersonates health: a failed pool renders as a named degraded note beside the verdict, never as a smaller number or "Nothing waiting." The fleet catalog is a first-class instrument — the search band's default mode is the hybrid catalog search agents use, and housekeeping shows catalog reach (entries per butler, stale rows, last write-behind, last decay sweep's fade/expire tally). Rows carry butler provenance marks, j/k triage and palette verbs cover register/validity switching, hover prefetches details, and Confirm/Retract/Restore form an honest, reversible commit vocabulary on every fact regardless of validity.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today the surface is a beautifully composed ledger over a lifecycle it cannot see: the decay sweep and catalog shipped, but the fading axis the whole page was designed around is a dead data contract (metadata.status written, validity read — fading is structurally 0 everywhere, dimming unreachable), forgotten rules still render and count as live standing orders, and the page's own degraded envelope (meta.pools_failed) has zero consumers while every fetch failure renders as calm emptiness ("Nothing waiting.", "The ledger is empty."). The red attention doors open onto lists with no root evidence (dead-letter error columns never serialized) and no levers (no requeue, no rule retirement, re-embed clears one pool of a fleet-wide count), and the fleet catalog is invisible — no search mode, no reach stats. The gap between this and the ideal is not layout or vocabulary (those are already close to world-class) but truth-wiring: one lifecycle contract, consumed degradation flags, evidence and agency behind every colored row, and catalog observability.

audits.ideal: The entities cluster is the household's memory made visible: the Plex opens as a five-second read of the owner's social field — who is close, who is drifting (desaturation), what needs attention (a rail whose cadence policy is the SAME server-side policy the relationship butler's proactive nudges run on, each rail item a door to the full overdue ledger) — and every failure names itself (a halo outage says 'dimensions unavailable', never a quietly emptier sky). The record page tells one truth from one fact spine: the store-labeled facts drill powers a 'Who they are' panel (identity facts: channels, dates, roles, verified marks) and a 'What happened' feed (narrative facts: interactions, gifts, loans), each row a door to its authoring session — no duplicate 'Facts' sections, no cross-store string joins, no block that hides identically for 'empty' and 'down'. Curation is keyboard-first and palette-discoverable (new/merge/pin/archive as ⌘K verbs), every destructive act is confirmed-or-undoable, and archive is a lifecycle with a visible archived shelf and an unarchive door — nothing the owner does is a one-way trapdoor. Credentials live on /secrets, one vocabulary of entity types governs every picker, and no section of the page survives a schema retirement it no longer serves.
audits.jarvis_gap: The Plex itself is near the bar — genuinely earned spatial memory, honest staleness/confidence axes, a real keyboard map — but the cluster around it leaks trust at the seams: the detail page carries a whole dead contact-era section that permanently tells the owner 'No linked contact' and force-opens an un-completable '(action needed)' owner-setup drawer (the contact-schema retirement never audited FE wiring); seven detail sub-blocks render outages as calm emptiness, so a down endpoint erases birthdays and activity indistinguishably from a quiet life; archive is a one-click disappearance with no archived view and an orphaned unarchive hook; the two fact stores surface as two different 'Facts' lists glued by a trimmed-string join; the attention policy lives only in frontend constants the butler cannot share; and none of it is on the palette-verb spine the rest of the console now runs on. Today's cluster is a strong canvas over a record page that still fabricates calm and preserves cruft the backend already buried.

audits.jarvis_gap: Today the secrets passport is the strongest credential surface in the fleet (tri-state honesty, capability probes, impact-gated destructive confirms, degraded notes), but it still fabricates calm at three seams: the cover headline ignores the system family entirely, the PageSystem heading band paints expired/expiring/never-probed system keys green, and the "last used"/recency axis is wired to a column the backend never writes. The settings console does honest per-subsystem degradation but reports a rolling-30d number as "Spend MTD" (contradicting the spend page's true calendar MTD and mis-firing the ceiling alarm) and is completely blind to credential health — the one subsystem whose failure silently kills butlers. The permissions page is a generation behind the fleet's shared primitives (raw fetch, hand-rolled state, silent flip failures, no URL vocabulary), several inbound doors drop or lie about their predicates (?tab=runtimes, "N more →" to /audit-log, /settings/models with no filter param), and ~700 lines of dead duplicate passport atoms — including two divergent ProviderMarks live on the same page — violate the zero-cruft bar.
audits.ideal: The ideal settings-and-secrets cluster is the trust anchor of the operator console: /settings opens as a five-second verdict over every governed subsystem — models, spend, approvals, permissions, and credentials — where each KPI is either a proven number or an explicit unknown, every attention item is a predicate-carrying door that lands on the exact failing row, and calendar-month spend means calendar-month everywhere. The secrets passport proves — never asserts — each credential's story along one unbroken spine: value fingerprint → live capability probes → real last-used consumption timestamps → audit stamps → /audit-log, with the same state vocabulary rendered identically on the spine, the KPIs, the headline, and the detail band, for all three families including system keys. Permissions, webhooks, models, and general locale settings are all editable through the same query-layer, keyboard-first, URL-addressable machinery as the rest of the fleet, and no dead atoms, dead filter states, or no-op affordances survive in the codebase.

findings.title: Settings console 'Spend MTD' is a rolling-30d sum, not month-to-date — mislabeled axis and false ceiling alarms
findings.detail: The console's spend_mtd_usd is computed from the '30d' rolling window, and the SpendPanel fetches /spend?period=30d then labels it 'MTD'. The spend-ceiling attention item compares this rolling sum against the monthly_usd ceiling, so early in a month it includes last month's spend and can fire 'Monthly spend is at N% of the ceiling' falsely. Meanwhile /api/spend/forecast computes true calendar MTD (month_start→today), so the console contradicts the spend page it links to. Failure-taxonomy shape 10 (mislabeled real data).
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/settings_console.py:184-188 ("30d" passed to _get_butler_session_stats*), :475-484 (ratio = spend_mtd / monthly ceiling); frontend/src/pages/SettingsConsolePage.tsx:91 (/spend?period=30d), :404 (label 'MTD'), :254 (KPI 'Spend MTD'); true MTD at src/butlers/api/routers/spend.py:1245-1248,1283

findings.title: Permission cell-flip failure is completely silent — privileged mutation with zero failure feedback

findings.title: ConsoleClock leaks its setInterval — cleanup function returned to setTimeout is discarded
findings.detail: The effect returns clearTimeout only; the inner '() => clearInterval(interval)' is returned from the setTimeout callback, whose return value goes nowhere. After the first minute boundary the interval survives unmount, ticking setState on an unmounted component forever and stacking one leaked interval per mount of /settings.

audits.jarvis_gap: Chronicles is close to the bar: editorial archetype, URL-backed day state, [/]/t shortcuts, never-blank floor, honest widget states — but its honesty spine has three holes (source-health query failures silently compose into a "quiet" headline, the feeder-honesty badge strip vanishes when its own query fails, and the day trail/scrubber silently truncates at 500 newest events). Education is the opposite pole and drags the pair down: it is a pre-Dispatch, Card-chrome page that never received the truth amnesty (page-level error renders as "No curriculums yet"), never received the design-language flip (the only raw light-only Tailwind palette chips left in the fleet), hides the butler's entire teaching-flow state machine and pending curriculum requests (both endpoints exist, both unwired), makes abandoned curricula permanently unreachable, and has no URL state, no doors from reviews to concepts, and no e2e/smoke coverage. The manifesto promises a live picture of learning; the page shows a static graph with invisible machinery behind it.

findings.title: Education page-level error impersonates the 'No curriculums yet' empty state
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/EducationPage.tsx:26 destructures only {data,isLoading} from useMindMaps; :70-90 renders EmptyState 'No curriculums yet. Request one to start adaptive learning.' whenever mindMaps.length===0 — which includes isError (data undefined). education-error-states.test.tsx covers only QuizHistoryList and MasterySummaryCards, not the page. Loading state is bare 'Loading...' text (:61-68), no skeleton, no Page primitive.
findings.detail: Failure-taxonomy shape 8/11 and a direct miss of the bu-86c4c truth amnesty: an API outage invites the owner to re-request a curriculum that already exists. The fleet's QueryBoundary/Page error convention was never adopted here.

findings.title: Chronicles briefing: source-health DB failure silently composes a 'quiet' day
findings.evidence: src/butlers/chronicler/editorial.py:479-480 — `except (asyncpg.UndefinedTableError, asyncpg.PostgresError): return items` swallows genuine failures (dropped connection, permission error) identically to a legitimately-missing table; compose_briefing_payload:787,802-803 then derives state_class/headline from the empty attention list, so the page headlines 'Yesterday was quiet.'
findings.detail: Violates the repo's own classify-before-flagging convention (CLAUDE.md degraded envelope, reference classifier _is_missing_memory_schema_error). Only UndefinedTableError should be treated as absent; any other PostgresError should surface a degraded attention item or flag on the briefing envelope so failure never impersonates calm on the page's biggest verdict surface.

findings.title: Education never received the Dispatch design-language flip — the last raw light-only palette chips in the fleet
findings.evidence: grep for bg-blue-100/bg-slate-100/bg-purple-100/bg-sky-100/bg-gray-100 across frontend/src hits ONLY education components: NodeDetailPanel.tsx:11-14, QuizHistoryList.tsx:13,18-20, CurriculumActions.tsx:18-19, ReviewTimeline.tsx:18-21 (border-l-red-500/amber-500/blue-500/gray-300). Violates openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md 'State Color Discipline' (exactly three token state colors) and 'Kind Tags' (mono uppercase, no background). Page also skips the Page shell/eyebrow/KPI primitives (EducationPage.tsx:63-104 hand-rolls h1 + Card grid) while 48 archetype references exist in ui/page.tsx.
findings.detail: Light-100 chips on the dark canonical theme, four bespoke tag palettes (purple=diagnostic, sky=teach, blue=good/reviewing/completed) that exist nowhere else in the instrument. Breaks 'one instrument built by one hand'.

findings.title: Abandoned curricula are permanently unreachable; the Re-activate affordance is dead code
findings.evidence: EducationPage.tsx:26 lists useMindMaps({status:'active'}) only; CurriculumActions.tsx:64-73 renders a Re-activate button for status==='abandoned', but no abandoned map can ever be selected from this page (the selector at EducationPage.tsx:107-118 is fed from the active-only list). After confirming Abandon, invalidation removes the map from the list while selectedMapId stays stale (auto-select effect :35-39 only fires when !selectedMapId), leaving the graph rendering a map the selector no longer names.
findings.detail: The abandon dialog promises 'Your progress will be preserved' (CurriculumActions.tsx:85) but the dashboard offers no door back — recovery exists only via Telegram prose. Failure-taxonomy shape 12 flavor: FE branches on a status value the page's own data source can never supply.

findings.title: Pending curriculum request is invisible and can wedge behind a permanent 409 with no recovery door
findings.evidence: roster/education/api/router.py:737-753 stores the request under the pending_curriculum_request KV lock and fires a detached session; no GET endpoint exposes the pending state (route list :152-713 has none) and no FE surface shows it. router.py:666-672 — if teaching_flow_start errors inside the spawned session the lock intentionally stays set, so every later request 409s ('already pending', use-education.ts:307-310) forever; the dashboard offers no way to see the stuck topic, jump to the failed session, or clear the lock.
findings.detail: Trace-spine break: request → session → mind map has no doors. The owner submits, gets a toast promising 'within a few minutes', and then the system goes dark; a single failed drain session bricks the feature until someone deletes a KV row by hand.

findings.title: Teaching-flow state machine (the butler's core loop) is invisible on the dashboard
findings.evidence: Backend GET /flows returns TeachingFlowResponse with phase state (roster/education/api/router.py:350-383); frontend hook useTeachingFlows exists (use-education.ts:216-222) but grep shows zero non-test callers. The manifesto's centerpiece — diagnostic calibration → planning → teaching → spaced review (roster/education/MANIFESTO.md:24-36) — has no rendering: the owner cannot see whether a curriculum is DIAGNOSING, stuck, or REVIEWING, nor when the next review session will fire for a map.
findings.detail: Backend-ready/frontend-not-wired (shape 5). Combined with the invisible pending request, everything between 'Request curriculum' and nodes appearing on the graph is unverifiable — the exact opposite of five-second verification.

findings.title: Chronicles day trail/scrubber silently truncates to the newest 500 point events
findings.evidence: ChroniclesDrilldownPanel.tsx:92 requests {limit:500}; roster/chronicler/api/router.py:255,287 caps limit at 500 and orders occurred_at DESC, so a day with >500 point events (OwnTracks + phone-activity + HA feeders) drops the morning. The response carries meta.total (:296) but the panel never reads it (:96-99), so the map trail and scrubber snap points render a partial day as the whole day.
findings.detail: Silent truncation (shape 7 flavor) on an evidence surface: the trail asserts 'where you were that day' while omitting its start. Either paginate to exhaustion for the settled-day window or render a 'trail truncated: N of M events' marker keyed off meta.total.

findings.title: SourceStateBadgeStrip — the feeder-honesty surface — vanishes when its own query fails
findings.evidence: SourceStateBadgeStrip.tsx:173 reads only {data} from useChroniclesSourceState(); :186 falls back to [] and :209 `if (!hasAnyBadge) return null`. A failed source-state fetch renders identically to 'no sources configured'. Same shape one level down: ChroniclesDrilldownPanel.tsx:96 ignores isError on useChroniclesPointEvents, so a failed events query renders as an empty map trail and snapless scrubber.
findings.detail: The one strip whose job is 'your feeders are broken' fails silent-benign (shape 11). Needs an inline SourceDegradedNote per the fleet convention.

findings.title: StrugglingNodesCard click has no visible effect (cross-tab dead door)
findings.evidence: EducationPage.tsx:121 Tabs is uncontrolled (defaultValue='curriculum'); StrugglingNodesCard lives in the analytics TabsContent (:159-162) and its onNodeClick only calls setSelectedNodeId — NodeDetailPanel that would display the node is in the unmounted curriculum tab (:134-138). Clicking a struggling concept from Analytics changes nothing on screen.
findings.detail: A real button wired to real data whose effect renders in a hidden tab — the click reads as broken. Fix: control the Tabs value and switch to curriculum (or render the detail panel as an overlay) on node click.

findings.title: ReviewTimeline: loading impersonates empty, and per-map query failures silently drop reviews
findings.evidence: ReviewTimeline.tsx:98-105 renders 'No reviews scheduled. Keep learning...' whenever allEntries.length===0 — true during initial load (mindMaps=[] while the list query is in flight) and when any/all of the N per-map queries error (:80 `reviewResults[i]?.data ?? []` with no isError/isLoading reads). Dates render via raw toLocaleDateString (:58) instead of the Time primitive; group colors are hardcoded Tailwind palette (:18-21).
findings.detail: The page's core promise ('review at the right time') is judged from this list; a partial fan-out failure shows fewer due reviews with total confidence. Rows are also not doors — an overdue review offers no path to its node, map, or a 'review now' action.

findings.title: Education analytics widgets: error states impersonate benign pending/nothing
findings.evidence: MasteryTrendChart.tsx:18-38 — query error leaves trendData empty and renders 'Analytics will appear after the butler computes its first daily snapshot' (error dressed as pending); CrossTopicChart.tsx:14-18 returns null on error AND while loading; StrugglingNodesCard.tsx:21-25 returns null on error, indistinguishable from 'no struggling concepts' (an all-clear).
findings.detail: Three more shape-8 instances in one tab; StrugglingNodesCard's silent null is the worst since absence reads as good news.

findings.title: Chronicles attention rows can collide on React keys
findings.evidence: ChroniclesPage.tsx:135-143 adaptAttention builds id `chronicles:${kind}:${title}`; editorial.py:775-784 emits one 'Long waking gap' item per gap with the identical title (severity 'low', detail varies), so two gaps in a day produce duplicate ids feeding AttentionList's key={item.id} (AttentionList.tsx:316,337).
findings.detail: Duplicate keys cause React reconciliation warnings/row misrendering exactly on multi-anomaly days. Include the index or detail in the adapted id.

findings.title: Education ignores the fleet poll-policy/event-bus discipline with ~10 hot polls on near-static data
findings.evidence: use-education.ts sets bespoke refetchInterval on every hook (30_000 at :30,41,50,61,86,211,221,229; 15_000 at :76) with zero imports from lib/poll-policy (grep confirms POLL_BUS_RECONCILE_MS is used by use-issues/use-timeline/use-approvals/use-butlers/use-sessions/use-spend but not use-education). Education data changes only when an ephemeral teaching session runs — a few times a day.
findings.detail: Post bu-qvnce.14, this page is the largest un-migrated polling island: mind-maps + mind-map + frontier + 2x analytics + cross-topic + quiz-responses + mastery-summary + N pending-review queries all re-poll every 15-30s.

findings.title: Education has no URL state and effectively one palette verb; dead hooks left as cruft
findings.evidence: EducationPage.tsx:29-31 selectedMapId/selectedNodeId/dialog are useState; Tabs :121 uncontrolled — no ?map=/?tab=/?node= (contrast ChroniclesPage.tsx:160-203 URL-backed date), so no deep link from anywhere (e.g. a Telegram digest) can land on a specific curriculum or concept. Orphaned exports with zero non-test callers: usePendingReviews (use-education.ts:70-77), useTeachingFlows (:216-222), useMindMapStrugglingNodes (:284-293, its dedicated /struggling-nodes endpoint router.py:545+ has no FE consumer — StrugglingNodesCard reads analytics.metrics instead), and useChroniclesAttention (use-chronicles-attention.ts:26, zero callers).
findings.detail: Breaks the bu-qvnce.13 predicate-carrying-doors convention and leaves two parallel sources for struggling-nodes (one wired, one dead) plus three dead hooks — compatibility cruft under the single-owner rule.

findings.title: Zero e2e/smoke coverage for /education and /chronicles
findings.evidence: grep over frontend/tests/e2e/ finds no spec touching '/education' or 'chronicles' (smoke.spec.ts has neither route); directory listing shows specs for spend, ingestion, secrets, entities, settings only.
findings.detail: A render crash on either page (the known new-field-with-stale-fixtures failure mode) would ship undetected; both pages depend on multi-source joins that are exactly the crash-prone shape.

findings.title: Mind map color/frontier semantics are undocumented on the graph
findings.evidence: MindMapGraph.tsx:21-27 encodes 5 mastery states as border colors and :37-41 a frontier halo ring, with no legend or key anywhere on the page; useFrontierNodes errors are ignored (:96) so frontier rings silently disappear on failure.
findings.detail: The manifesto calls the mind map 'your learning territory... what you know, what you are working on, and what comes next' (MANIFESTO.md:29-31); the owner must reverse-engineer the color code to read it.

audits.ideal: The ideal surface is a matched pair of evidence instruments. /chronicles stays the editorial archive it already is, but every layer of its honesty spine survives its own failure: a source-health or point-events query failure renders a named degraded note (never a quiet headline, never a vanished badge strip), the day trail declares truncation when it cannot show the whole day, and every KPI cell and attention row is a door into the gantt/drawer below the fold. /education becomes the same instrument speaking Dispatch: an editorial-console page whose opening line answers "is my tutor working?" — a KPI strip (due reviews, mastery, streak, estimated completion), a per-curriculum lifecycle rail showing the live teaching-flow phase (diagnosing → planning → teaching → reviewing) with a door from each phase to the session that ran it, a pending-request row from the moment of submission (with an unwedge action if the drain session dies), URL-addressable curriculum/concept state so the Sunday digest can deep-link straight to a struggling node, and reviews that are doors — every overdue row one keystroke from its concept dossier and one from "review now". Nothing on either page is rendered that the system cannot prove, and nothing the system does (a request, a flow transition, a review scheduling) is invisible to the owner.

audits.jarvis_gap: Today /qa is a well-composed dossier shell (DispatchVerdict opener, KPI strip, URL filters, patrol pulse) and /system opens with a computed verdict — but the trust spine underneath has holes: resetting the QA circuit breaker fabricates a fake 'clean' patrol and a fake case that then render as real system activity everywhere (the exact moment the system is at its worst is repainted as healthy); the breaker toolbar and butler-detail chip assert "closed" when the summary fetch fails; a QA case dossier has no door to the investigation session (the signal→session→audit spine dead-ends at the case); the QA-self meta-review lane and the trends endpoint exist on the wire but no surface renders them; the /system verdict is blind to the QA staffer entirely, so a halted self-repair loop never reaches the owner's five-second check; and the case rail lacks the j/k triage, pagination, and palette verbs its sibling surfaces already earned. The gap is not features — it is that the QA surface, whose whole identity is honesty about failure, still contains fabrication paths and severed evidence doors.

findings.title: Circuit-breaker reset fabricates a 'clean' patrol + a case that render as real activity across /qa
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/qa.py:3161-3195 inserts a synthetic qa_patrols row (status='clean', completed_at=now()) plus a 'manual_reset' healing_attempts row. Downstream: summary last-patrol query has no exclusion (qa.py:1284-1292) so the synthetic patrol becomes last_patrol and staffer_status flips to 'healthy' (qa.py:1530-1535) with last_patrol_at = the reset moment — masking a real errored last patrol; stats_24h.patrols_completed counts it (qa.py:1305); all-time success_rate is diluted because total_dispatched counts status != 'dispatch_pending' (qa.py:1474-1482); /cases includes the synthetic attempt (qa.py:1869 'a.qa_patrol_id IS NOT NULL') and state_of_case falls through to 'detect' (src/butlers/core/qa/severity.py:44-60), so a permanent low-sev 'CircuitBreakerReset in dashboard' case appears at the top of the rail; the patrol pulse strip renders the synthetic patrol as a green clean dot (frontend/src/pages/QaOverviewPage.tsx:325-332,345-363).
findings.detail: The reset fires precisely when the system has 5 consecutive investigation failures — and its side effect is to render 'QA staffer healthy: last patrol just now' plus a green patrol dot for a patrol that never ran. Direct violation of 'failure never impersonates health / nothing fabricated'. The new toolbar control (commit 69e990d95) puts this one confirm-click from the primary surface. Fix: first-class breaker-reset state (dedicated table or a marker row excluded from every patrol/case/summary/stats query), not a forged patrol.

findings.title: Breaker control asserts 'Circuit breaker closed' when the summary source is loading or failed
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/QaOverviewPage.tsx:496 `const breakerTripped = summaryData?.circuit_breaker.tripped ?? false;` — summary.isError/isLoading → button renders 'Circuit breaker closed' (lines 238-248), while the QaVerdictOpener directly below the same toolbar renders 'QA summary unavailable' from the same failed query (QaVerdictOpener.tsx:71). Same shape in frontend/src/components/butler-detail/ButlerQaInvestigationsTab.tsx:486-503: CircuitBreakerChip ignores isError and `status?.tripped ?? false` renders the green 'Circuit breaker: closed' badge on fetch failure.
findings.detail: The just-landed toolbar (69e990d95) has two states (closed/tripped) where the truth has three (closed/tripped/unknown). Neither test in the commit covers the summary-error case. Held to the bar: render an 'unknown' state when the feeding source is loading or errored.

findings.title: QA case dossier has no door to its investigation session — trace spine severed
findings.evidence: The /cases/{id} SELECT omits healing_session_id and session_ids (src/butlers/api/routers/qa.py:1974-2022); QaCaseDossier type has no session field (frontend/src/api/types.ts:5236-5246); `grep -rn "session" frontend/src/components/qa/*.tsx` returns zero hits. Meanwhile HealingAttempt (types.ts:4993-4995) carries session_ids/healing_session_id and useHealingAttempt exists but has no consumer.
findings.detail: From a QA case the owner cannot reach the investigation session (the SessionDossier that already carries trace_id/stderr from the 07-04 epic), nor the source butler session that produced the failure — the signal→session→audit→root-evidence chain dead-ends at the case. This is the flagship trace-spine surface and it is the one missing the doors.

findings.title: Reset endpoint: non-transactional double INSERT, no evidence shown at confirm time, no palette verb
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/qa.py:3169-3195 — two separate pool.execute calls with no transaction: a failure after the first leaves an orphaned fabricated 'clean' patrol while the breaker stays tripped. FE confirm is a bare window.confirm (QaOverviewPage.tsx:446) with zero context; GET /api/qa/circuit-breaker returns recent_attempts/recent_statuses (qa.py:3114-3127) but nothing on /qa consumes them (the only consumer is ButlerQaInvestigationsTab.tsx:486). Palette registration covers only force-patrol (QaOverviewPage.tsx:462-474).
findings.detail: The operator resets blind: the five failing attempts that tripped the breaker are on the wire but never shown. The shipped impact-aware-confirm pattern (secrets v2) and useModalChoreography are unused here. Reset should show the failure chain, run in one transaction, and be a registered palette verb while tripped.

findings.title: /system verdict is blind to the QA staffer and self-repair state
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/system/SystemVerdictBanner.tsx:52-142 composes only board/instance/backups/insights/posture; no useQaSummary/useQaCircuitBreaker source. findings.title: Meta-review lane (QA-self-recursive findings) is backend-only — the 'operator lane' never reaches the operator

findings.detail: Findings about the QA staffer itself are deliberately diverted from auto-investigation (correctly, to prevent recursion) into a lane no surface renders — so QA's own defects rot invisibly. Failure taxonomy shape 5. Render a meta-review section/strip on /qa or delete the endpoint.

findings.title: qa.py is a 3,468-line monolith router
findings.evidence: wc -l src/butlers/api/routers/qa.py → 3468; one file mixes circuit-breaker math, GitHub PR client calls, investigation-notes parsing, dossier assembly, meta-review, repo settings, synthetic findings, and force-patrol MCP fan-out.
findings.detail: Largest router in the API layer; split into a package (summary/cases/patrols/breaker/settings) matching the endpoint groups its own docstring already enumerates.

audits.ideal: The QA + System pair is the household's internal-affairs desk: /system opens with one verdict that unions every source that can hurt the owner — fleet liveness, backups, posture, insights, connectors, AND the staff's own repair loop — where every clause is a door and an unreachable source is named, never calm; /qa opens with the staffer's honest tri-state (healthy / tripped-with-the-five-failures-shown / unknown-because-the-feed-is-down), a patrol history that distinguishes running, clean, suppressed, and failed and never vanishes on error, and a case rail with j/k triage, pagination, and palette verbs; every case dossier walks the full spine — finding → investigation session (one keystroke to the SessionDossier with trace_id and stderr) → PR → merge — and QA's findings about itself land in a visible meta-review lane; the circuit breaker is first-class state whose reset is a transactional, audited, impact-aware act that changes nothing about recorded history, so nothing on the surface ever renders a patrol that did not run or a case that was not a defect.

findings.title: Routing-failed events ('failed' status) are invisible on the entire timeline — the failure surface hides real failures
findings.detail: public.ingestion_events.status='failed' is a real, live value: ingestion_event_mark_failed sets it on routing failures (core/ingestion_events.py:788-797) and it is called from the live dispatch reconcile path (switchboard_wiring.py:237, core_tools/_switchboard.py:296); the replay endpoint explicitly supports replaying 'failed' rows (core/ingestion_events.py:955-961). But the FE vocabulary omits it everywhere: IngestionEventStatus (api/types.ts:3515-3522) and ALL_STATUSES (TimelineTab.tsx:221-229) have no 'failed'; the client-side filter `events = allEvents.filter((e) => enabledStatuses.has(e.status))` (TimelineTab.tsx:2036) silently drops any 'failed' row even when every chip is on; the built-in 'errors' view statuses ['error','replay_pending','replay_failed'] (TimelineTab.tsx:177) exclude it; RowStatus/ROW_STATUS_WORDS have no entry (StatusBadge.tsx:141-166); and the backend histogram assembly drops 'failed' counts on the floor in its defensive else branch (core/ingestion_events.py:702-709, _HISTOGRAM_STATUSES at :190-197 lacks 'failed'), so hour totals under-count too. A dispatch that failed after ingestion — the single most important thing this ledger exists to show — cannot be seen, filtered, or replayed from the UI. Failure taxonomy shape 12 (backend-wide vs frontend-narrow vocabulary).
findings.evidence: core/ingestion_events.py:792-793,959; switchboard_wiring.py:237; frontend/src/api/types.ts:3515-3522; frontend/src/components/ingestion/TimelineTab.tsx:177,221-229,2036; frontend/src/components/ingestion/StatusBadge.tsx:141-166; src/butlers/core/ingestion_events.py:190-197,702-709

findings.title: Connectors roster renders fabricated calm on fetch failure: 'No connectors registered.' + all-zero KPI verdict
findings.detail: ConnectorsRoster destructures only { data, isLoading } from useConnectorSummariesWithAggregates (ConnectorsRoster.tsx:122-123); isError is never read and no QueryBoundary wraps the page. On an initial-load failure (backend outage, navigation with cold cache) allConnectors=[] renders the honest-empty copy 'No connectors registered.' (:207), an empty AttentionStrip, and a KPI footer asserting 'connectors · live 0 / healthy 0 / needs attention 0 / auth · error 0 / events · 24h 0' (:229-249) — a full all-clear verdict the system cannot prove. Same shape in FiltersPipeline: on a failed active-rules fetch, rulesError is only passed to ChannelDefaultsBlock (FiltersPipeline.tsx:370) while all five GateSections render 'No rules at this gate. Policy lives in code.' from the empty fallback (FiltersPipeline.tsx:141, GateSection.tsx:112-116). Shapes 8+11; violates the fleet-wide honest-aggregation convention this same page partially adopts (SourceDegradedNote for hourly/device sources but not for the primary query itself).

findings.title: Connector detail: all four secondary sources fail to benign — stats→'no throughput recorded', events→'No recent events.', incidents→'No incidents recorded.', rules→'No routing rules reference this connector.'
findings.detail: ConnectorDetailPage reads only .data from useConnectorStats, useConnectorEvents, useConnectorIncidents, useConnectorRoutingRules (ConnectorDetailPage.tsx:104-124); no isError is consumed and undefined is coerced to null (:250-252). On a stats failure, deriveSparkline returns Array(24).fill(0) (ConnectorDetailView.tsx:626-637) and ConnectorHistogram renders the explicit 'no throughput recorded' empty state (ConnectorHistogram.tsx:41-63) — a failure impersonating a deliberately-honest quiet-day state. Events/incidents/routing failures render the calm empty copies (ConnectorDetailView.tsx:476-482,525-531,574-580). 'No incidents recorded' on a failed incidents query is exactly the moment fabricated calm matters most. Shape 11 (failure-degrades-to-benign across a multi-source join); page-level error handling covers only detailError (:210-221).

findings.title: Fabricated system-policy prose: '3 retries with exponential backoff' asserted in two places; no such policy exists in code
findings.detail: GATE_DEFS execute gate: gloss 'Failures retry up to 3 times, then queue for replay' and codePolicy 'Exponential back-off, 3 retries, then manual replay queue' (gate-state.ts:77-79). EventDrawer replay tab: 'Retry policy: up to 3 attempts with exponential backoff, then held for manual review.' (EventDrawer.tsx:527-529). Verified against code: the dispatch pipeline hardcodes attempt:1 at every fanout site (modules/pipeline.py:1982,2603,2905, no retry loop); the replay executor drain_replay_pending is single-attempt, marking replay_complete/replay_failed once (connectors/filtered_event_buffer.py:155+); the only max_attempts:3+backoff policy in the repo is outbound webhooks (api/routers/webhooks.py:72), unrelated to ingestion. The dedupe gate's 'Window: 90s for sensor data, 24h for content' (gate-state.ts:59) is also suspect: no such constants found, and an open bead notes dedupe_key/dedupe_strategy are NULL on all 171k rows. This is copy inherited from the graduated prototype JSX presented as live system fact — shape 4, direct violation of 'nothing fabricated'.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/ingestion/filters/gate-state.ts:59,77-79; frontend/src/components/ingestion/timeline/EventDrawer.tsx:527-529; src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:1982,2603,2905; src/butlers/connectors/filtered_event_buffer.py:155-230; src/butlers/api/routers/webhooks.py:72

findings.title: Connector lifecycle spine severed: pause/run-now backend endpoints have zero FE callers, and a paused connector would render as healthy 'online / authorized'
findings.detail: POST /api/ingestion/connectors/{type}/{identity}/pause and /run-now are fully implemented with audit entries and 409 semantics (ingestion_connectors.py:576-700+), per the lifecycle-gate-matrix spec. Zero frontend callers exist (grep across frontend/src finds none); ConnectorDetailView carries onPause/onRunNow props that render 'pause poll'/'run now' buttons (ConnectorDetailView.tsx:127-129,372-393) but ConnectorDetailPage never passes them (ConnectorDetailPage.tsx:246-255), so the buttons never mount — shape 5 (backend-ready, frontend-not-wired) plus dead props. Worse, pause writes state='paused' and run-now writes state='unknown' (ingestion_connectors.py:605,679-684), but deriveConnectorDispatchInfo branches only on 'error'/'degraded' (connector-auth.ts:66-152) — 'paused' and 'unknown' fall through to the healthy path, so a paused connector would show a green dot, 'online', and 'oauth · authorized' on the roster (shape 12). The FE type comment even documents the narrow domain: state: string // "healthy" | "degraded" | "error" (api/types.ts:3309).
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/ingestion_connectors.py:576-700; frontend/src/components/ingestion/connectors/ConnectorDetailView.tsx:127-129,372-393; frontend/src/pages/ConnectorDetailPage.tsx:246-255; frontend/src/components/ingestion/connectors/connector-auth.ts:66-152; frontend/src/api/types.ts:3309

findings.title: Ingestion cluster has zero adoption of the shipped shared primitives: no list triage, no poll-policy tokens, no event-bus invalidation, no prefetch-on-intent
findings.detail: useListTriage (j/k/enter keyboard triage) is adopted on Dashboard/Approvals/Issues/Notifications but not on the ingestion ledger — the densest, highest-frequency triage list in the app (grep: no useListTriage/useRegisterShortcut in components/ingestion or pages/Ingestion*). use-ingestion.ts and use-ingestion-events.ts use raw refetchInterval literals (30_000/60_000/120_000; use-ingestion.ts:98,117,139; use-ingestion-events.ts:113) and are absent from eslint's POLL_POLICY_FILES enforcement set (frontend/eslint.config.js:221-227); no bus-driven invalidation exists for a surface whose whole point is 'what just arrived'. Row-level replay updates rely on a 30s poll plus manual optimistic overrides. Keyboard path from the ledger: no j/k, no shortcut to toggle status chips or range, selection only via shift-click/checkbox.

findings.title: 'events · today' means two different things on roster vs detail — same label, different axis and source
findings.detail: The summaries endpoint computes today.messages_ingested as the trailing-24h sum of hourly_events from public.ingestion_events (ingestion_connectors.py:136-139,415-420, explicitly '24h window'). The connector detail endpoint computes today_messages_ingested as calendar-day (received_at >= CURRENT_DATE) heartbeat counter deltas from connector_heartbeat_log (roster/switchboard/api/router.py:1164-1182). ConnectorDetailView labels it 'events · today' (ConnectorDetailView.tsx:236-238) while the roster's KPI band says 'events · 24h' fed by the other axis. Walking roster→detail for the same connector shows two disagreeing numbers under near-identical labels — shape 10 adjacent (axis mismatch across sibling surfaces), erodes trust in both.

audits.ideal: The ingestion cluster is the house's sensory ledger: every external signal, its verdict, and its downstream consequence on one unbroken spine. The timeline surfaces the complete status vocabulary the backend can emit — including routing failures — with a keyboard-triaged ledger (j/k/enter, palette verbs for range/view/replay), bus-driven freshness instead of blind 30s polls, and hour strips whose counts either come from a live histogram or say plainly that the histogram is down. The connectors roster is a five-second fleet check where every number is provable: a failed summaries fetch renders as a named outage, never as 'no connectors'; a paused connector says paused; the attention derivation is one function shared by roster, timeline strip, and detail. Connector detail is the operational cockpit its spec promised: live pause/run-now with audit trail, a histogram carrying the same ingested+filtered series as the roster, per-source degraded notes when events/incidents/rules queries fail, one consistent 'events' axis from list to detail, and a purpose line drawn from the catalog, not string-mangled from the type name. Filters describe only policies that exist in code, citing real constants — no prototype prose about retry windows the system never implements — and every gate count is measured, estimated-and-marked, or absent.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today the surface is rich and mostly honest at the component level — URL-backed filters, trace scoping, audited payload reads, saved views, skip-aware sparklines, and device liveness are genuinely world-class touches — but it fails the doctrine exactly where failure matters: the one status that means 'dispatch failed after ingestion' ('failed') is invisible across chips, ledger, errors view, and histogram; a dead backend or failed secondary query renders as calm ('No connectors registered', 'No incidents recorded', 'no throughput recorded'); the filters page and event drawer assert a 3-retry exponential-backoff policy that does not exist in code; and the connector lifecycle (pause/run-now) is a severed spine with dead props on one end, uncalled endpoints on the other, and a paused state that would render green. The shipped shared primitives (list triage, poll-policy tokens, event bus, palette verbs) have zero adoption here despite this being the hottest triage list in the app.

findings.title: bu-qvnce.11's binding half is unshipped on 10 of 13 verb-registering scopes — palette verbs with no keyboard path and an empty '?' sheet
findings.detail: bu-t64p2 (closed) promised 'register palette verbs (with bindings via useRegisterShortcut) on calendar, memory, secrets, qa, spend, health, education, butler-detail, settings, chronicles'. The reachability half shipped, the binding half did not: SpendPage (2 scopes), QaOverviewPage, EducationPage, HealthOverviewPage, SettingsConsolePage, SettingsModelsPage, SettingsPermissionsPage (3 scopes), memory HousekeepingBand, secrets DirectionPassport, and ButlerDetailPage(+Actions) all call useRegisterCommands but set zero `binding` fields and register zero shortcuts — grep for 'binding' across all of them returns only ApprovalsPage.tsx:1373. Only Approvals, Calendar, and Chronicles pair both registries. Consequences: (a) the palette's kbd column (EntityFinder.tsx:891-903) renders on ~6 commands fleet-wide, so 'the palette is where shortcuts are learned' is untrue on most pages; (b) the '?' sheet's 'On this page' section (shortcut-hints.tsx:113-123) is empty on Spend/QA/Memory/Secrets/Health/Education/Settings/ButlerDetail — the majority of surfaces; (c) where pairing DOES exist, every verb is hand-defined twice (CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:4144-4199 and ChroniclesPage.tsx:215-284 duplicate label/perform vs description/handler and binding vs display), a drift-prone shape the two-registry design imposes. Unifying mechanism: one `useRegisterAction({id, label, binding?, description?, perform})` that emits the palette entry, the key handling, and the '?' hint from a single declaration (command-registry.tsx:44-54 already documents the manual pairing as a known seam), plus a test asserting every PaletteCommand.binding has a live matching ShortcutBinding.

findings.title: Empty-query palette Actions window is starved by 13 always-registered 'Trigger <butler>' commands — page verbs invisible in the browsable state
findings.detail: EntityFinder shows `allActions.slice(0, 8)` at empty query (EntityFinder.tsx:442-443) with no ranking: order is scope-insertion order of the registry Map (command-registry.tsx:94 flattens Map.values()). GlobalActionsRegistrar registers one 'Trigger <name>' command per roster butler (~13, GlobalActionsRegistrar.tsx:35-57) at layout level and never unregisters; a page's scope is deleted and re-appended on every navigation, so after the first route change every page scope sorts AFTER the global scope. Net effect: the browsable empty-query Actions group — the exact surface bu-qvnce.11 built so 'verbs are visible before the first keystroke' — shows 8 near-identical Trigger commands and drops the contextual page verbs (Approve next, Create event, Jump to today, spend rules...) entirely. Unifying mechanism: give registry scopes a priority tier (page > global) or have useCommandMenuActions interleave page scopes first; alternatively collapse the 13 trigger verbs into one 'Trigger butler…' command with a sub-picker.

findings.title: Route-registry orphans recurred: /ingestion/connectors and /ingestion/filters are unreachable from palette, g-chords, and the '?' sheet — and no parity test guards the class
findings.detail: route-registry.ts's stated purpose is 'so /entities/circles and the six health sub-pages can never be orphaned again' (route-registry.ts:48-50), but the first-class ingestion sub-routes added since (router-config.tsx:171-172) are in neither SIDEBAR_ROUTES nor EXTRA_ROUTES: the palette Pages group cannot navigate to Connectors or Filters, the '?' sheet doesn't index them, and only the /ingestion tab bar reaches them. The regression class the registry was built against has already re-occurred once, because route-registry.test.ts only pins the historical orphan list (route-registry.test.ts:17-71) — there is no parity test deriving expected coverage from router-config's static, non-redirect routes. Unifying mechanism: export the static route table from router-config and assert every non-redirect, non-parameterized path appears in ALL_ROUTES or an explicit exemption list.

findings.title: The entity workbench's container-scoped keyboard maps (EntityDetail m/j/k/e/Shift+Backspace, EntitiesIndex, Plex) are advertised nowhere — the shortcut registry has no publication-only mode
findings.detail: EntityDetailPage installs a rich view-local keyboard map (m merge-review, j/k step entities, e rename, Shift+Backspace forget, Esc back — EntityDetailPage.tsx:2746-2755) bound to the page root by design ('NEVER to window'); EntitiesIndexPage (EntitiesIndexPage.tsx:1143,1536) and PlexPage's graph canvas (PlexPage.tsx:1955-1961) do the same. Because useRegisterShortcut couples publication to window-global installation, these deliberately focus-scoped maps cannot use it, so they appear in neither the '?' sheet's 'On this page' section nor any on-page kbd chip (grep kbd|KbMono across all three files → zero hits). Some of the fleet's deepest keyboard interactions are tribal knowledge readable only in source comments. Unifying mechanism: split publication from installation — `useShortcutHints(bindings)` (or an `installEnabled: false` flag on useRegisterShortcut) so container-scoped maps publish to the help sheet while keeping their own focus-scoped handlers; add a one-line kbd legend to the Plex canvas and Index list headers.

findings.title: EmptyState's `action` slot is dead weight: ~1 of 39 call sites offers the filling action, so a fresh instance teaches nothing
findings.detail: The canonical EmptyState supports an `action` node (empty-state.tsx:9,55,66) and the design-language rule it cites is 'state the fact, then offer the next action' — but across 39 non-test call sites only EducationPage.tsx:78 (plus the Page primitive passthrough, page.tsx:491) passes one. Everything else is passive-voice waiting copy: 'Butlers appear here when they connect' (RegistryTable.tsx:47-48), 'Entities appear as the butler builds the knowledge graph' (EntitiesIndexPage.tsx:657-658), 'No sessions found' (SessionTable.tsx:115-116). For system-fed ledgers passive is honest, but user-fillable surfaces (chat ConversationList, calendar connect, ingestion connectors, contacts) have a real verb available and don't surface it — and since there is no other first-run experience anywhere (grep onboarding|first-run|Welcome → nothing), empty states ARE the first-run experience and they currently teach nothing actionable. Mechanism: classify each EmptyState call site as system-fed vs user-fillable; require `action` (or a door to the connector/setup surface) on the user-fillable tier, enforceable by a lint-style test on the classification list.

findings.title: Two divergent key-cap primitives: Kbd (filled, shortcut-hints.tsx) vs KbMono (transparent hairline, KbMono.tsx)
findings.detail: The '?' help sheet and the list-triage footer strip render keys with `Kbd` (bg-muted filled chip, shortcut-hints.tsx:47-53; imported by list-triage-footer.tsx:18), while the command palette's binding column and footer render `KbMono` (transparent, hairline --border-strong, KbMono.tsx:27-45). Same semantic object — a keyboard key — drawn from two visual vocabularies, in the two surfaces a user compares side by side when learning a shortcut. Mechanism: collapse to one primitive (KbMono is the token-compliant one per its Brief citation) and re-export it from ui/, deleting the local Kbd.

audits.ideal: The shell's discoverability spine is one declaration deep: a page states each verb once — id, label, key binding, description, handler — and that single declaration simultaneously (1) installs the key handling, (2) surfaces the verb in the command palette with its kbd chip, (3) publishes it to the '?' sheet's "On this page" section, and (4) renders the page's footer hint strip; container-scoped keyboard maps (Plex, entity workbench) publish hints through the same channel without installing global handlers. The palette's browsable empty-query state leads with the current page's verbs, then recents, then global fleet verbs. Every static route is provably indexed in the one route registry (parity-tested against the router), every badge-carrying hot page has a g-chord, and every chord is advertised on the sidebar item itself. Empty states on user-fillable surfaces carry the door that fills them, so a fresh instance teaches its own setup path. One key-cap primitive renders every keyboard hint in the product.
audits.jarvis_gap: The mechanisms are genuinely world-class in design — single route registry feeding sidebar/palette/chords/help-sheet, split-context command and shortcut registries, recents, fuzzy ranking, modal choreography — but adoption is roughly half-shipped and nothing enforces it: 10 of 13 verb-registering scopes have palette entries with no keyboard binding and an empty '?' "On this page" section (bu-t64p2 closed with its binding half undelivered); the browsable empty-query Actions window shows 8 of 13 global "Trigger <butler>" rows and drops the contextual page verbs; the ingestion sub-routes have already re-orphaned from the route registry with no parity test to catch the recurrence; the fleet's richest keyboard maps (entity detail/index/Plex) are structurally unpublishable because the registry couples hints to window-global installation; and the sidebar never shows a chord. Today the tenth use still needs the mouse on most pages, and the first use on a fresh instance is taught by passive "items appear here" copy with a dead `action` slot.

audits.jarvis_gap: The Dispatch base layer genuinely flipped: tokens, ButlerMark registry, chart-colors channels, Row/Eyebrow/Pill/KpiStrip/StateDot primitives, and three eslint guard families all exist, and flagship surfaces (Overview, Calendar workspace, Secrets passport) speak the language fluently. But the app today is bilingual, not unified: a second shadcn dialect (solid state-color badge fills in 13 files, 4 parallel status-badge components, rounded-full pills, ring-based focus in 100+ sites vs 2 spec-conformant ones, two normative type scales in index.css itself) coexists with Dispatch, and ~165 var(--token, oklch-literal) fallbacks quietly re-invent token values — several wrong (amber hue 70 vs 84, an --mfg fallback carrying --dim's value, four distinct greens). Worse, some shared primitives contradict the spec they cite: ui/Pill is rounded-full while CalendarWorkspacePage hand-rolls the correct 3px-radius pill twelve times; calendar-overlays.ts maintains a second, contradictory butler-hue mapping (rose = health in ButlerMark, rose = relationship in overlays). The ideal 'one instrument built by one hand' needs the mechanism layer (guards + codemods) extended to the gaps the current guards deliberately or accidentally skip: .ts files, cool hues, oklch literals, and the primitives' own spec drift.

findings.title: calendar-overlays.ts maintains a second, contradictory butler-hue mapping (hue with two meanings)
findings.evidence: frontend/src/lib/calendar-overlays.ts:110-122 overlayButlerAccent(): finance=emerald, travel=sky, relationship=rose, health=violet — but ButlerMark's canonical registry (spec § Butler Category Hues) assigns health=--category-5 which IS rose, relationship=--category-10 raspberry, finance=--category-3 amber, travel=--category-11 indigo. Rose therefore means 'health' on every letter-mark and 'relationship' on calendar overlays. Also violates 'the hue SHALL appear only on the butler's letter-mark' (spec.md:114-120), using raw Tailwind classes (emerald/sky/rose/violet) that the status-color eslint guard misses (cool hues unguarded).
findings.detail: chart-colors.ts already exports butlerHueVar() as the sanctioned entry point for by-butler coloring. Delete the hand mapping; either route through butlerHueVar (with a spec amendment permitting overlay accents) or drop butler accents to neutral border+ButlerMark, which the spec already prefers.

findings.title: ~165 var(--token, oklch-fallback) literals re-invent token values outside index.css; several are wrong
findings.evidence: grep across src: 88 spaced + 77 unspaced 'var(--x, oklch(...))' sites. Mismatches: connector-auth.ts:175-209 and GoogleHealthStatusCard.tsx:45-49 use var(--amber,oklch(0.72_0.12_70)) — hue 70 vs token hue 84, matching neither theme (index.css:99,492); var(--red,oklch(0.62_0.20_25)) x18 matches neither 0.627/29.2 nor 0.685/29.2; four distinct green fallbacks exist (0.72_0.17_150 x8, 0.65_0.15_145, 0.790 0.195 148, vs tokens 0.50/152 light and 0.790/148 dark); secrets/passport/atoms.tsx:25 'var(--mfg, oklch(0.55 0 0))' — the fallback for --mfg is --dim's value.
findings.detail: Violates spec § Surface Palette scenario 'raw color literals appear only in the token definition file itself' (spec.md:73-76). The fallbacks are dead code — every token is unconditionally defined at :root — so their only possible runtime effect is rendering a WRONG color. The existing HEX_COLOR_SELECTORS guard (eslint.config.js:96-110) doesn't catch oklch( literals. Mechanism: codemod-strip all fallbacks; add an eslint selector banning oklch(/rgb(/hsl( literals in src outside index.css and lib/contrast.

findings.title: Solid state-color badge fills in 13 files; four parallel status-badge components for one concept; blue invented as a fourth state color
findings.evidence: grep 'bg-\[var(--green)\] text-white': 13 files incl. components/butler-detail/ButlerStatusBadge.tsx:34, components/ingestion/StatusBadge.tsx:47, components/schedules/ScheduleTable.tsx:189, components/notifications/notification-feed.tsx:57, components/layout/Sidebar.tsx. ingestion/StatusBadge.tsx:66 uses bg-blue-500 for replay_pending (a fourth state color; spec.md:78-86 'exactly three state colors exist'). Dialects: sessions/StatusBadge.tsx (dot+label, token-correct), ingestion/StatusBadge.tsx (solid fills), butler-detail/ButlerStatusBadge.tsx (solid green fill), ui/live-status-badge.tsx — same concept, four stylings.
findings.detail: Spec § State Color Discipline: state color 'never on background fills — foreground or border only' (spec.md:91-97,100-103); § Status Indicators mandates StateDot with four canonical states (spec.md:266-273). replay_pending maps naturally to 'waiting' (muted). Mechanism: one shared StatusTag primitive (StateDot + mono label) in ui/, delete the other three; eslint selector banning bg-[var(--red|--amber|--green)] when combined with text-white.

findings.title: Focus contract effectively unimplemented: spec's 2px --fg outline exists at 2 sites; two competing ring dialects at 100+
findings.evidence: grep counts: 57 sites shadcn 'focus-visible:ring-ring/50 ring-[3px]' (ui/button.tsx:8, ui/badge.tsx:8), 45 sites 'focus-visible:ring-2' (mostly ring-[var(--fg)]/30, e.g. ui/Pill.tsx:82, CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:931), 2 sites outline-based; index.css contains no :focus-visible rule at all (grep 'focus-visible' index.css → no matches). Spec.md:336-341: 'Focus is visible — 2px outline of --fg at 2px offset — via :focus-visible only.'
findings.detail: Single highest-leverage unification: one global rule in index.css (@layer base :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--fg); outline-offset: 2px }) plus removing per-component ring classes makes every current and future interactive element conformant by default — keyboard-first doctrine depends on it. A 30%-alpha ring is materially weaker than the spec's full-contrast outline.

findings.title: Two normative type scales coexist in index.css; 788 arbitrary-px text sites and ~12 eyebrow tracking dialects fill the gap
findings.evidence: index.css:229-251 defines a 1.2-ratio --text-* scale remapping Tailwind (xs=11.1px, sm=13.3px, 2xl=27.6px) while spec.md:151-162 mandates integer steps 10/11/13/14/16/24/32/44. Result: text-[9px]/[10px]/[11px]/[13px] arbitrary values appear 788 times because no Tailwind step matches Dispatch sizes. Eyebrow dialects: canonical is 10px/0.14em (ui/Eyebrow.tsx:37-40) but inline tallies show 36x tracking-widest, 31x text-xs tracking-wide, 27x 0.12em, 20x 11px tracking-wider, 18x 0.08em, 12x 0.1em, 11x 9px — ≥12 distinct combos, ~163 files with inline 'uppercase tracking-wide'.
findings.detail: Mechanism: retire the 1.2-ratio scale and remap Tailwind font-size tokens onto the Dispatch px table so utilities and spec agree and arbitrary values become lintable; codemod inline eyebrows to <Eyebrow>; extend the PRIMITIVE_REDECLARATION-style guard to inline 'uppercase tracking-' combos outside components/ui/.

findings.title: ui/Pill contradicts the spec's pill button; CalendarWorkspacePage hand-rolls the conformant pill ~12 times
findings.evidence: spec.md:246-253: pill = '4px 10px / 1px border / 3px radius / mono 11px; active state is inverted bg/fg'. ui/Pill.tsx:66-78: 'h-6 rounded-full px-2.5', mono text-[10px] tracking-wide, selected = fg text + fg border (not inverted). CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:812,1030,1341,1835,4436 etc. build 'rounded-[3px] border px-2.5 font-mono text-[11px]' inline — the spec pill, rebuilt per call site, never generalized.
findings.detail: The shared primitive is the off-language one while the conformant pattern lives as page-local class strings. Rewrite ui/Pill to the spec shape (3px radius, 11px mono, inverted active), migrate calendar's inline copies onto it, plus range-toggle.tsx (rounded-md container) onto the same shape.

findings.title: Chronicles lane palette: 9 duplicated Tailwind-class + raw-hex pairs, off-token, theme-blind, reusing state hues categorically
findings.evidence: components/chronicles/lane-taxonomy.ts:96-154: each lane carries colour:'bg-slate-500' AND hex:'#64748b' that 'must visually match' by hand; eat = #f59e0b, byte-identical to the --amber/--severity-medium state token (index.css:99); rest = emerald-600. AggregatePieChart.tsx:387 feeds lane.hex into recharts fill — same hex in dark and light mode, unlike every category token which has theme variants (index.css:165-176 vs 519-530). eslint.config.js:85-90 scoped the hex guard away from .ts 'out of this bead's diff size' — deferred, not settled.
findings.detail: Mechanism: define --lane-* tokens (or map lanes onto the --category ramp via categoryHueVar) with dark/light variants, drop the hex field (chart code reads var() via chart-colors helpers), and extend HEX_COLOR_SELECTORS to **/*.ts — the '.ts can't contain JSX' rationale (eslint.config.js:334-337) holds for the redeclaration guard but not for hex Literals; .ts data modules are exactly where hex hides.

findings.title: Tailwind palette-class eslint guard covers only warm hues; 26 files keep off-token cool-hue colors, mostly 'blue = interactive' meaning drift
findings.evidence: eslint.config.js:58-67 STATUS_COLOR_SELECTORS regex bans only (red|green|emerald|amber|yellow|orange). Survivors: pages/ApprovalsPage.tsx:132 text-blue-600, components/timeline/TimelineLedger.tsx:54-56 bg-blue-500/bg-purple-500 channel dots, components/relationship/UnlinkedEntitiesSection.tsx:155,227 bg-blue-50/bg-blue-950 tinted panels, PendingIdentitiesSection.tsx:162, schedules/ScheduleTable.tsx:151 bg-blue-600/90, qa/PRPanel.tsx:27 sky, ingestion/StatusBadge.tsx:66 blue, general/JsonViewer.tsx (6 hits), education/QuizHistoryList.tsx (4 hits) — 26 files total.
findings.detail: Dispatch has no accent hue: interactivity is underline + fg (spec.md:333-336), so 'blue = link/info' is a meaning the language deliberately lacks. Mechanism: extend the guard regex to all Tailwind hues (blue|sky|violet|purple|rose|pink|cyan|teal|indigo|slate|zinc|fuchsia|lime), migrate the 26 files to tokens or neutrals, keeping the line-level-disable escape for true categorical palettes.

findings.title: State-color tinted callout boxes bypass the .attention-row contract — including the shipped shared SourceDegradedNote primitive and a green tint no rule permits
findings.evidence: components/ui/query-boundary.tsx:136 SourceDegradedNote: 'border-[var(--amber)]/40 bg-[var(--amber)]/10' rounded box — tint without the .attention-row rail contract (index.css:665-672 is the sole sanctioned tint: red/amber, tint+rail as one unit); components/butler-detail/GoogleHealthStatusCard.tsx:113 red/10 banner; components/butler-detail/RuntimeConfigCard.tsx:120 amber/10 box; components/education/CurriculumActions.tsx:17 'bg-[var(--green)]/10 text-[var(--green)]' — a GREEN background tint, outside even the red/amber-only exception (spec.md:90-98).
findings.detail: Each was built ad-hoc; together they form a second, unsanctioned attention-tint dialect — one of them inside a bu-qvnce-shipped shared primitive. Mechanism: add a sanctioned .attention-note class (tint+rail, red/amber only) to index.css with a matching spec amendment and migrate all four, or restyle to left-rail + foreground color only. CurriculumActions' green tint becomes a StateDot regardless.

findings.title: Radix overlay primitives ship forbidden zoom/scale-in motion on every dialog, sheet, and dropdown
findings.evidence: components/ui/dialog.tsx:68 'data-[state=closed]:zoom-out-95 data-[state=open]:zoom-in-95' (same family in alert-dialog.tsx, dropdown-menu.tsx, sheet.tsx slide) — spec.md:315-330: the motion vocabulary has four entries, none a dialog, and 'scale-in' is explicitly forbidden. The bu-86c4c.6 fix (dialog.tsx:64-67) corrected duration/easing but left the zoom; the global reduced-motion floor only covers users who opt out.
findings.detail: Strip zoom-*/slide-* from the shared overlay primitives leaving the 200ms fade, or amend the spec's motion table with an 'overlay fade 200ms' entry — one decision applied once in ui/ covers every consumer.

findings.title: Chat TypingIndicator uses forbidden animate-bounce; the language already has a sanctioned 'composing' affordance
findings.evidence: components/chat/TypingIndicator.tsx:10-18: three dots with animate-bounce staggered 0/150/300ms. spec.md:325-326 forbids bounce explicitly; spec.md:296-304 defines the Process Status Pill 'composing…' (amber) as the honest system-is-working signal.

findings.title: KPI stat-tile dialect: font-bold text-2xl tiles bypass KpiStrip, and notification stats color healthy totals green/red decoratively
