findings.evidence: components/butlers/BoardHeader.tsx:13,97 renders 'text-2xl font-bold tracking-tight' citing 'design-language.md H1 standard' — doctrine (about/heart-and-soul/design-language.md:260-263) says the standard is text-3xl owned by <Page>, and the Dispatch Title is 44px/500 (components/ui/page.tsx:153-163); pages/EducationPage.tsx:64,73,96 triplicates the same hand-rolled h1 across loading/error/ready branches; components/butler-detail/ButlerDetailHeader.tsx:156 is a fourth copy.

findings.title: Health MeasurementChart colors a generic data series with the butler identity hue — cross-wiring channels chart-colors.ts itself forbids
findings.evidence: components/health/MeasurementChart.tsx:149,360-380: useCategoryHue() resolves the health butler's hue and feeds it as line stroke for measurement series; lib/chart-colors.ts:4-8 header: 'never use a butler hue for a generic series'. Sibling surface components/butler-detail/ButlerHealthMeasurementsTab.tsx:341 renders the same kind of data with chartColor() — same data, two dialects across surfaces.
findings.detail: The series is not colored by-butler as a dimension (one butler on the page); switch to chartColor() so the rose hue stays exclusive to the health letter-mark.

audits.ideal: Every surface compiles from one visual grammar with zero dialects: a single normative token file where the Tailwind utility scale IS the Dispatch type/spacing table (no arbitrary-px escape hatch needed), every color reference resolves to a token with no inline fallback literals, one status affordance (StateDot/StatusTag) with exactly four states, one pill, one eyebrow, one focus outline declared globally, one butler-hue registry consulted by charts, calendars, and marks alike, and a motion vocabulary of four entries enforced at the shared-primitive layer. The eslint guard layer is hue-complete and file-type-complete so any new off-language color, tracking value, or animation fails CI before review — the language maintains itself, and the operator console reads as one instrument built by one hand at 3am in either theme.

moves.title: Token-integrity sweep: strip var() fallback literals, ban oklch/hex literals repo-wide, extend palette guard to all hues and .ts files
moves.why: Spec § Surface Palette: 'raw color literals appear only in the token definition file itself' (spec.md:73-76); doctrine 'one hand' — today ~165 fallback literals (several wrong: amber hue 70 vs 84, --mfg fallback = --dim value) and three deliberate guard gaps (cool hues, .ts files, oklch literals) let drift compound silently. Payoff: color drift becomes structurally impossible, not review-dependent.

findings.title: Two freshness regimes fight on bus-covered pages: legacy 10-15-60s primary polls override the event bus's reconcile cadence
findings.detail: SessionsPage mounts a pre-bus, user-facing AutoRefreshToggle (localStorage, default 10s) and passes it into FOUR bus-covered queries, overriding useSessions' POLL_BUS_RECONCILE_MS default — the flagship sessions surface polls at 10s while the bus already invalidates ["sessions"] on every session event. SpendPage does the same to useDailySpend (60s override of a bus-covered key). use-timeline-ledger keeps a permanent 15s head poll and use-ingestion-events a permanent 30s poll on keys the registry invalidates (timeline/ingestion patches). The AutoRefreshToggle knob itself is compatibility cruft from before EventBusProvider existed; with compat waived it should be retired, and the 'honest floor when the socket is down' rationale (use-timeline-ledger.ts:26-29) solved once by bus-health-adaptive intervals rather than per-page fast floors.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/SessionsPage.tsx:123,154,176,188,198 (useAutoRefresh(10_000) piped into useSessions/useSessionAggregate etc. whose default is POLL_BUS_RECONCILE_MS at hooks/use-sessions.ts:46); frontend/src/pages/SpendPage.tsx:1370 (refetchInterval: 60_000 override of useDailySpend, bus-covered per event-cache-registry.ts:73-78); frontend/src/hooks/use-timeline-ledger.ts:29,71 (HEAD_POLL_MS=15_000); frontend/src/hooks/use-ingestion-events.ts:113 (30_000 default on a key ingestionPatch invalidates, event-cache-registry.ts:157-161); frontend/src/hooks/use-auto-refresh.ts:12-40

findings.title: Bus health is exposed but no query adapts to it — socket-down silently degrades bus-covered surfaces to 5-minute (or infinite) staleness
findings.detail: EventBusProvider exposes status/lastEventAt, but the only consumer outside the provider is RootLayout's indicator. Every hook demoted onto POLL_BUS_RECONCILE_MS (sessions, approvals, spend, board, issues, messenger, timeline) keeps the 5-min sweep even while the socket is dead, and use-notifications.ts has NO refetchInterval at all — bus-only, so a dropped socket leaves notifications frozen until window refocus. The 'five-second fleet verification' bar quietly becomes minutes of staleness with only a small shell indicator as the tell. The unifying mechanism nobody built: a useBusAwarePollInterval(fallbackMs) hook returning POLL_BUS_RECONCILE_MS while status==='open' and a fast fallback (15-30s) while degraded, adopted by every bus-covered hook — which also removes the justification for the permanent fast floors in finding 1.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/lib/event-bus.tsx:60-135 (status/lastEventAt in context); grep 'useEventBus' → only frontend/src/layouts/RootLayout.tsx:68 consumes it; frontend/src/hooks/use-notifications.ts has zero refetchInterval/POLL lines (grep output); frontend/src/lib/poll-policy.ts:23 (fixed 5-min constant, no bus-awareness)

EpisodesRegister has the identical shape. findings.title: Infinite-query interval refetch storm: 30s polls refetch ALL loaded pages, and use-ingestion-events' comment claims first-page-only behavior that TanStack v5 does not have
findings.detail: useIngestionEvents (refetchInterval 30s) carries the comment 'Refetch only the first page at the interval' — but v5 infinite queries refetch every loaded page sequentially on interval (refetchPage was removed; no maxPages set anywhere in the repo). useChroniclesEpisodesInfinite does the same deliberately. An owner who pages deep into ingestion history or chronicles gets O(loaded-pages) serial requests every 30s for as long as the tab is open. Fix: maxPages, or generalize use-timeline-ledger's head/committed split (separate live head query + frozen history pages) which was built once for the timeline and never extracted.

findings.title: Palette 'Trigger <butler>' gives no acknowledgment until the POST returns and has no in-flight dedupe — a paid action that can double-fire
findings.detail: GlobalActionsRegistrar's perform() awaits triggerButler (session spawn, easily >1s) with the palette already closed; nothing on screen acknowledges the action until the success/error toast. Per the latency-budget bar, >300ms actions need immediate acknowledgment and >1s needs visible progress. Reopening the palette (recents surface the action first) and pressing Enter again fires a second session — real spend. ButlerDetailActions solved both (isRunning guard) but the guard was never generalized to palette-performed network actions. Fix: toast.promise('Triggering <butler>…') fired synchronously in perform(), plus a per-command in-flight set in the command registry so network-backed verbs are repeat-safe by construction.

findings.title: Optimistic-mutation primitive adopted in only 4 of ~90 mutation files; its own doctrine mandates classifying all 238 sites, and clear OPTIMISTIC-class toggles still roundtrip
findings.detail: use-optimistic-mutation.ts's module doc says every useMutation call site should be classified OPTIMISTIC vs HONEST-PENDING. Meanwhile toggle/pin-class mutations that the doc's own taxonomy names as OPTIMISTIC remain plain roundtrips: ingestion rule enable/disable toggle, timeline saved-view create/update/delete (pin). No mechanism records the classification, so the sweep can never be verified complete. Fix: one classification pass over the 238 sites; convert the toggle class via useOptimisticListMutation; record HONEST-PENDING verdicts as a required comment tag the eslint rule (or a grep-based test) checks on every useMutation call.

findings.title: Prefetch-on-intent registry covers 3 routes while the handlers are attached everywhere — EntityFinder's own primary destination (/entities/:id) gets no warmth
findings.detail: usePrefetchOnIntent is wired into RowLink, DisclosureRow, and the palette's highlighted result, but resolvePrefetchTarget maps only /sessions/:id, /approvals/:id, /timeline. Entity detail — the palette's flagship destination and the hottest hover-then-open loop — plus butler detail, fact/episode/rule detail, connector detail, and notification detail all resolve to null, so the 120ms intent timer fires into a no-op. The registry hand-rolls regex matchers instead of deriving from route-registry.ts, so growth means writing a new matcher per route rather than declaring queryKey+queryFn alongside the route. Fix: move prefetch descriptors onto route-registry entries (or export key+fn pairs from each detail hook) and map the top hover-navigated detail routes.

audits.ideal: Under the interaction-speed lens, the ideal Butlers dashboard has exactly one freshness architecture: the fleet event bus is the primary update path for everything it covers, a single named reconcile cadence backs it up, and every poll interval in the codebase is a named policy token whose meaning (primary vs reconcile vs static) is lint-enforced repo-wide; when the socket drops, every bus-covered query automatically tightens to a fast fallback so honesty about staleness is structural, not a shell badge. Every parameter-keyed list keeps its previous rows visible while refetching (never a false empty-state), every reversible toggle/ack/pin is optimistic through the one shared primitive with each mutation site carrying its recorded OPTIMISTIC/HONEST-PENDING verdict, every network-backed palette verb acknowledges within 100ms and is repeat-safe, and hover/focus intent warms the cache for every detail route the owner actually navigates to — all guaranteed by registries with coverage tests rather than by convention.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today the primitives are all built and all excellent — EventBusProvider with a declarative cache-patch registry and coverage manifest, poll-policy tokens with an eslint rule, usePrefetchOnIntent with a route registry, useOptimisticMutation with a written classification doctrine, a never-blank placeholderData floor — but each stopped at a beachhead: the lint covers 9 files while ~97 raw-literal poll sites sit in 23 others; the prefetch registry maps 3 routes while its handlers are attached fleet-wide; the optimistic primitive lives in 4 of ~90 mutation files; bus health is exposed but nothing adapts to it, so SessionsPage still runs a pre-bus 10-second auto-refresh knob against bus-covered queries while notifications would freeze entirely on a dropped socket; and the memory browser flashes 'The ledger is empty.' on every filter click. The gap is not missing machinery, it is adoption discipline plus one missing keystone (bus-aware poll intervals) — the difference between a JARVIS that is instant everywhere by construction and one that is instant on the five pages someone hand-tuned.

moves.title: useBusAwarePollInterval: adapt every bus-covered query's interval to socket health, then retire the legacy fast floors and the AutoRefreshToggle
moves.why: vision.md's five-second fleet verification and 'failure never impersonates health': a dead socket today silently means 5-minute (notifications: infinite) staleness, while healthy sockets carry redundant 10-15-60s polls that exist only as socket-down insurance (use-timeline-ledger.ts:26-29 says so explicitly). One hook — POLL_BUS_RECONCILE_MS while status==='open', ~15-30s fallback while degraded — makes both problems structurally impossible and lets SessionsPage's pre-bus AutoRefreshToggle (compat cruft, waived) be deleted.

findings.title: Clickable table rows use <tr role="button"> — destroys table semantics for screen readers on the sessions ops surface
findings.detail: SessionTable renders every interactive row as <TableRow role="button" aria-label="Open session detail for ..."> with aria-selected. role="button" on a <tr> (a) overrides row semantics so the 11 data cells (time, model, complexity, duration, status, tokens, cost) collapse into a single button whose accessible name is the aria-label — the actual cell data becomes unreachable column-by-column in a SR table reader; (b) aria-selected is not a permitted attribute on role=button (axe aria-allowed-attr violation); (c) the pattern is duplicated on the relationship watchlist <tr>. The codebase already built the canonical alternatives (RowLink for navigation, DisclosureRow for expand/collapse) but has no mechanism preventing new raw role="button" rows: SettingsConsolePage tiles hand-roll div role=button navigation instead of RowLink, and CirclesPage/EpisodesRegister/TimelineLedger hand-roll expand rows instead of DisclosureRow (beyond bu-f310e's facts/rules/audit scope).
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/sessions/SessionTable.tsx:166,174-180 (aria-selected + role=button + aria-label on TableRow); frontend/src/components/butler-detail/ButlerRelationshipContactsTab.tsx:383-392 (<tr role=button>); frontend/src/pages/SettingsConsolePage.tsx:292-302 (div role=button nav, RowLink exists at src/components/ui/RowLink.tsx:2); frontend/src/components/relationship/CirclesPage.tsx:354-365, src/components/memory/EpisodesRegister.tsx:148-160, src/components/timeline/TimelineLedger.tsx:185-195 (hand-rolled disclosure rows; DisclosureRow exists at src/components/ui/DisclosureRow.tsx:54)

findings.title: FloatingChatWidget: role="dialog" with zero focus choreography, no Escape — and its mere presence suspends every page-scoped shortcut app-wide
findings.detail: The chat panel carries role="dialog" but adopts none of useModalChoreography: no focus-in on open, no Escape-to-close, no focus restore (the trigger button unmounts while open, so focus is dropped to <body> when opened by keyboard). Worse, isShortcutTargetSuspended() suspends ALL useRegisterShortcut bindings whenever document.querySelector('[role="dialog"]') matches — the chat widget is a NON-modal side panel the owner keeps open while working, so opening chat silently kills j/k triage, approvals a/d/x, and every other page shortcut across the whole app until the panel is closed. Two shipped bu-qvnce.10/.11 primitives actively fight each other.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chat/FloatingChatWidget.tsx:348-354 (role=dialog, no onKeyDown/choreography; grep for Escape/keydown in file returns nothing), :497-500 (trigger unmounts while open); frontend/src/hooks/use-register-shortcut.tsx:147 (document.querySelector('[role="dialog"]') suspends all bindings); useModalChoreography adopter list excludes the widget (grep useModalChoreography → TimelineEventDrawer, ButlerManagementTab, EntityFinder, CalendarAgendaView only)

findings.title: Global shortcuts (/, ?, g-chords) lack the open-dialog guard the page-scoped registry has — g+key navigates the router underneath open modals
findings.detail: useKeyboardShortcuts guards only editable fields (INPUT/TEXTAREA/contentEditable). It does not check for open dialogs, unlike isShortcutTargetSuspended in the page-scoped registry. With a Radix Dialog/AlertDialog open (merge review, destructive confirms, butler management modal), pressing g then a letter navigates the page underneath the modal (unmounting it mid-decision), '/' stacks the EntityFinder palette on top of the open modal, and '?' opens the help sheet over it. The two keyboard registries — built to 'read as one family' — enforce different suspension rules.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-keyboard-shortcuts.ts:17-70 (no dialog check anywhere; g-chord at :55-69 fires on any non-editable target); contrast with frontend/src/hooks/use-register-shortcut.tsx:135-149 (SUSPENDED_TAGS incl. SELECT + role=dialog check)

findings.title: useListTriage j/k selection is invisible to screen readers and can move off-screen — the flagship keyboard interaction has no non-visual signal
findings.detail: The shared triage hook (adopted on Approvals, Dashboard AttentionList, Issues, Notifications) moves a pure state cursor: no DOM focus move, no aria-activedescendant, no announce(), no scrollIntoView. A SR user pressing j/k hears nothing (selection is only a bg-muted class + aria-selected on a role where it may be invalid); verbs (a/d/x) then act on a row the user was never told about. Even sighted keyboard users can drive the selection below the fold silently (no adopter calls scrollIntoView). The shell announcer shipped in the SAME bead (bu-qvnce.10) and is used by only 3 call sites — the two primitives were never wired together.

findings.title: Live streams have no SR narration: chat streaming replies and running-session dossiers update silently
findings.detail: MessageThread renders streaming assistant content with zero live-region semantics — no role="log" on the thread, no aria-live on the streaming message or the TypingIndicator, no announcement when a reply completes; a SR user who sends a message gets no feedback that a reply is arriving or has arrived. SessionDossier polls live data for running sessions (elapsed tick, process_log/stderr) with no aria-live/role=log either. The focus-run doctrine ('dynamic results are announced') is met by the ingestion drawer (local role=status span) and NewEventsPill but not by the two most conversational live surfaces.

findings.detail: The bu-qvnce.10 completeness check is structurally sound, but coverage itself is frozen at 3 real axe passes (ButlersPage, ButlerDetailPage, TimelineTab component-level). skip-manifest.ts has exactly one commit (the shipping PR #2916, 07-04) and all 30 entries remain, most saying 'lift the hook-mock list from X.test.tsx' — i.e. mechanical work nobody scheduled. There is also no ratchet: the manifest can stay at 30 forever and the suite stays green, and dynamic detail routes (/sessions/:id dossier, /entities/:id, connector detail) are outside ALL_ROUTES entirely, acknowledged in the test header as a future 'sibling registry' that doesn't exist.

findings.title: Amber severity glyphs painted with --severity-medium — the exact 2.01:1 light-theme value the contrast audit fixed under a different token name
findings.detail: The bu-86c4c.16 contrast pass minted --amber-text because base amber measured 2.01:1 on light --bg, but only repointed text-[var(--amber)] sites. AttentionList's '~' warning glyph and RollupTrendWidget's flag glyph use color: var(--severity-medium), which index.css documents as the SAME oklch(0.769 0.189 84) value — so the dashboard's warning marker renders at ~2:1 in light theme, below even the 3:1 graphics floor. contrast.test.ts's TEXT_TOKENS list (dim, amber-text, fg, mfg, green) never covers the severity/role/state/permanence token families even where they're used as glyph/text color, so alias-shaped regressions are structurally invisible to the test.

findings.title: Five JS smooth-scroll call sites bypass the global reduced-motion floor
findings.detail: index.css's prefers-reduced-motion floor sets scroll-behavior: auto !important, but per CSSOM-View an explicit scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth'}) in JS overrides CSS scroll-behavior — so calendar jump-to-event, entity-detail drawer reveal, chat autoscroll, and both timeline scroll-to-row paths still animate for reduced-motion users. The comment above the CSS floor even claims the JS hook remains 'the right tool' for canvas/SVG only, missing this class. No shared scroll helper exists.

findings.title: role="alert" used as a static error STYLE across 32 sites — page loads with degraded sources fire simultaneous assertive announcements
findings.detail: The honest-aggregation doctrine was implemented by putting role="alert" on persistent, render-time error/degraded content (QueryBoundary error branch, every AttentionList error row, OperationsNowList degraded rows, calendar panels, ErrorState primitive). Because React mounts these after document load, SRs treat them as dynamically-added alerts and announce each assertively — a dashboard with several degraded sources interrupts the page-title announcement with an alert storm on every navigation, teaching SR users to ignore alerts. role=alert should be reserved for failures appearing after user action; render-time degraded notes belong in polite status text plus one coalesced shell announcement.

audits.ideal: Accessibility on this console is a property of the registries, not of individual conscientious components: the same route registry that drives the sidebar and palette drives a full axe sweep (top-level and detail routes, skip manifest empty or shrinking under a ratchet); one suspension guard governs both keyboard registries so modal, non-modal, and inline surfaces each get exactly the shortcut behavior their role declares; every overlay declares itself through useModalChoreography or Radix and nothing else; every clickable row is RowLink, DisclosureRow, or a real in-cell control inside intact table semantics, enforced by lint; the shell announcer narrates everything the pixels say — triage cursor moves, streaming replies, degraded sources (once, coalesced, politely) — so keyboard-first and screen-reader-first are the same product; and the token contrast test covers every token family that ever lands in a color: position, both themes, with reduced-motion honored by CSS floor and JS helpers alike.
audits.jarvis_gap: The bu-86c4c/bu-qvnce epics built genuinely excellent accessibility *infrastructure* — useModalChoreography, the shell announcer, the registry-driven axe completeness check, the token contrast test, the global reduced-motion floor, RowLink/DisclosureRow primitives — but adoption stalled the day they shipped: the axe skip manifest has never lost an entry (3/33 routes covered), the announcer has 3 call sites, the choreography hook has 4 adopters while the chat widget (a role=dialog that silently disables every page shortcut app-wide) uses none of it, the two keyboard registries enforce different modal guards, the flagship j/k triage interaction is inaudible to screen readers, the sessions table erases its own table semantics with tr role=button, and the contrast fix missed the identical amber value hiding behind the --severity-medium alias. Today it is a set of world-class parts wired into perhaps a third of the product; the ideal is those same parts made structural — lint rules, ratchets, and cross-wiring so the next surface inherits accessibility instead of re-deciding it.

audits.ideal: Every hot file is readable on first pass: the dispatch money path (spawner) reads as a short orchestrator calling named phase functions (resolve model, apply spend rules, enforce gates, invoke with failover, record ledger); each module lives in a package with tools as module-level, directly-testable functions and a thin register_tools that only wires decorators; the frontend API layer is split per domain so a calendar PR never conflicts with a secrets PR; pages are composed from sub-components and custom hooks under ~400 lines each; shared helpers (DB manager dep, cost formatting) have exactly one definition; no parameter exists that no body reads, and no production branch exists to defend against test mocks.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today the highest-churn files are also the least decomposed: 156 backend functions exceed 150 lines (spawner._run 1,408L, pipeline.process 1,395L, calendar register_tools 2,274L), the two most-edited files in the repo (frontend/src/api/types.ts at 8,246L/204 commits and client.ts at 6,947L/161 commits since May) are single-file conflict magnets, and CalendarWorkspacePage's default export is a single 4,457-line component with 30 useState hooks. The repo already contains its own counter-examples — modules/memory/ is a package, calendar_workspace.py router is well-factored into ~40 small helpers, lib/format-cost.ts and api/deps.py exist — but the hot paths never adopted those precedents, so every new feature lands as another 100 lines inside an already-monolithic function, and 61 copies of _get_db_manager plus three byte-identical formatCost clones show duplication is the default under time pressure.

findings.title: spawner._run is a 1,408-line money-path monolith with phase-crossing mutable locals
findings.detail: The function that executes every LLM dispatch runs ~10 sequential phases (context prep, catalog resolution, spend-rule routing, permissions gate, quota-skip loop, monthly ceiling, MCP warmup, invoke+failover, session_complete, ledger-in-finally) in one body. Cross-phase mutable flags (_failover_already_classified, preconsumed_runtime_tool_calls, _ledger_input_tokens et al. set mid-function and consumed in the finally block) mean a reader must hold the whole 1,400 lines to predict behavior of any one phase. Violates code-readability bar #2 (one thing at one altitude) and #7 (state scoped tightly) on the system's most failure-prone path.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/spawner.py:873-2281 (function span from AST scan: 1,408 lines); phase-crossing locals at spawner.py:896-910 (preconsumed_runtime_tool_calls, _failover_already_classified) and spawner.py:904-910 (_ledger_* tokens consumed in finally); phase map via grep: spend-rules comment block ~:986, quota-skip loop ~:1037, monthly ceiling ~:1167

findings.title: Production code defends against test MagicMocks in the dispatch path
findings.detail: spawner._run validates the catalog resolution result with a 10-line tuple-shape guard whose comment explicitly says it exists to reject 'a MagicMock from a test pool that does not stub the catalog tables'. Test-fixture deficiencies are being patched in production control flow; the correct fix is stubbing the catalog in the test pool fixture and deleting the guard (fail-fast bias #6, readability bar #3 — a reader cannot tell whether this branch encodes a real runtime possibility).

findings.title: Main check job red since 2026-07-06: wall-clock time-bomb in entity-activity binning test
findings.evidence: roster/relationship/tests/test_entities_api.py:58 freezes `_NOW = datetime(2026, 5, 18, ...)`; test at :1990-2009 seeds facts at _NOW-40d and asserts 3 nonzero bins, but the endpoint anchors its 90-day window at real wall clock (roster/relationship/api/router.py:6302 `today = datetime.now(UTC).date()`). Reproduced locally 2026-07-10: `uv run pytest roster/relationship/tests/test_entities_api.py::TestEntityActivityBinning::test_bins_only_returns_dense_90_day_series` → `AssertionError: assert 2 == 3` (the _NOW-40d = 2026-04-08 fact aged out of the window). CI: gh run 28888877607 (main, 07-07) check=failure at step 'Integration tests (testcontainers)', same failures 07-06 (run 28762155318); no open PR or bead covers it (gh pr list + bd list checked). Next detonation: _NOW-5d ages out ~2026-08-11, _NOW itself ~2026-08-16.
findings.detail: Violates test-rigor expectation 6 (deterministic or quarantined) and, worse, demonstrates that a red `check` on main goes unnoticed for 3+ days (bu-xotdv covers only frontend-e2e not being required; `check` is equally unprotected — `gh api .../branches/main/protection` returns 404 Branch not protected). Every PR run since 07-06 inherits this red, training the fleet to ignore the integration step. The file's docstring also lies about its own marker (see next finding), which is why a mocked-pool test failed inside the testcontainers step.

findings.title: roster/conftest.py force-marks 1,469 declared-unit mocked tests as integration — marker taxonomy corrupted
findings.evidence: roster/conftest.py:42-44 `pytest_collection_modifyitems` adds `pytest.mark.integration` + docker-skipif to EVERY test under roster/. 46 roster test files declare `pytestmark = pytest.mark.unit` (1,469 test functions, counted via grep), e.g. roster/relationship/tests/test_entities_api.py:51 whose docstring (:31) explicitly claims 'pytestmark = pytest.mark.unit (not the Docker-guarded roster integration mark)' — false in effect: CI's Unit step (-m "not integration", ci.yml:119) excludes them and the testcontainers job (ci.yml:223) runs them.
findings.detail: Consequences: (a) 1,469 pure-mock tests execute in the expensive testcontainers job (12m23s) instead of the unit step; (b) locally without Docker they are skipped entirely despite needing no Docker; (c) any integration-coverage statistic counts them (my raw count of 'integration' test functions was 2,686 — over half are actually mocked); (d) the explicit `unit` marker anywhere under roster/ is dead lettering, so authors' declared intent is silently overridden. Fix: make the conftest auto-mark respect an explicit unit marker (or only auto-mark files importing testcontainers fixtures) and update scripts/check_integration_coverage.py expectations.

audits.ideal: A green run certifies the system: every test is deterministic (no wall-clock anchoring against frozen fixtures — a nightly clock-skew leg proves it), every marker tells the truth about what a test needs (unit means no Docker, integration means real Postgres, and CI's collection guard keeps both exhaustive), the fleet's honesty conventions (degraded envelope, JSONB bind discipline) are enforced by contract-tier tests and grep gates so a new endpoint physically cannot regress them silently, the FE/BE contract is a generated OpenAPI artifact that fails CI on drift and types every e2e fixture, and flakes are measured in a ledger rather than absorbed by retries — so that a red main is rare, loud, and acted on within hours, and a green main is earned calm the operator can actually trust.

audits.jarvis_gap: Doctrine states the boundary rules with unusual clarity (about/heart-and-soul/architecture.md: modules never touch core, MCP-only inter-butler communication with RFC-gated exceptions, deterministic daemon, anti-pattern list explicitly banning un-RFC'd cross-schema access and butlers importing each other's code), but the actual import graph violates them systemically: ~25 upward core/modules/jobs->butlers.api imports whose own comments admit they hide circular dependencies; a fleet event bus whose daemon-side producers publish into in-process queues that structurally cannot reach the dashboard-api process (silent event loss masked by polling — failure impersonating health); domain butlers bypassing the Switchboard MCP hop that RFC 0011 calls its core anti-spoofing guarantee; a shared module doing un-RFC'd cross-schema WRITES into chronicler's schema; and the framework's most stable layer (core/scheduler, identity, core_tools) importing per-butler roster code via an import-time sys.modules injection hack. The ideal — dependencies pointing one way, every doctrine exception carrying its RFC — is fully articulated in the repo's own documents; the code just doesn't keep the promise.
audits.ideal: Every boundary in about/heart-and-soul/architecture.md is enforceable and enforced: butlers.api is a pure interface layer importing downward only (pricing, audit append, conversation store, and DatabaseManager live in core/shared packages); daemon-originated live events cross the process boundary via a real transport (Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY) instead of dying in in-process queues; every cross-schema access is a migration-tracked read-only view per RFC 0010 or has its own RFC amendment; insight candidates enter only through the MCP tool with unspoofable origin identity exactly as RFC 0011 promises; the switchboard routing engine is either framework (in src/) or roster (behind a registered interface), not both at once; and an import-linter contract in CI makes each of these directions a build failure rather than a code-review hope.

findings.title: Fleet event bus is dead across the process boundary: daemon-side emit_* calls publish to in-process queues whose only subscribers live in the separate dashboard-api container
findings.detail: emit_event/emit_spend_event/emit_approvals_event maintain module-level subscriber lists and ring buffers (api/routers/events.py:74-76, spend.py:107-127, approvals.py:80-87). WS subscribers exist only in the dashboard-api process (docker-compose.yml:205-214, command ["dashboard",...] -> cli.py:231 uvicorn api.app). But the producers for session, spend, notification, approval-created, and ingestion events run in the butlers-up container (docker-compose.yml:548-551): core/sessions.py:330-343 (session ended), core/spawner.py:2237-2260 (per-call spend), core_tools/_notifications.py:973-984 (notify delivery), modules/approvals/gate.py:428-441 and email_guard.py:161-176,403 (approval created). Every such event lands in an empty subscriber list and is discarded; failures log at debug only. The dashboard's Live indicator still shows connected (API-side heartbeats, events.py:16-20) and polling masks the loss — live streams silently carry only API-process-originated events. Also each producer import is an upward core/modules->api edge, with comments explicitly admitting the hidden cycle ('Lazy import avoids a circular dependency: core -> api', spawner.py:2235, sessions.py:326-329) — the exact cycle-hiding pattern the dependency bar bans.

findings.title: RFC 0011's core guarantee is not implemented: domain butlers bypass the MCP-only entry point and origin_butler is a spoofable string parameter
findings.detail: RFC 0011 states propose_insight_candidate() 'is the sole entry point for candidate submission, enforcing Rule 3', that 'origin_butler is set by the broker from the calling butler's MCP session identity. Butlers cannot spoof their origin', and that direct writes are 'prohibited by Rule 3'. In code, finance/health/travel roster jobs import the switchboard's broker function directly and call it in-process — a butler importing another butler's roster code, the architecture doc's named anti-pattern ('Allowing butlers to import each other's code'). The broker signature takes origin_butler as a plain caller-supplied argument. health_jobs.py's own docstring admits the shortcut ('pending cross-butler MCP wiring'). No RFC amendment documents this exception.

findings.title: Memory module performs un-RFC'd cross-schema WRITES (UPDATE/DELETE) into chronicler.episode_entities during entity merge
findings.detail: modules/memory/tools/entities.py runs SELECT, UPDATE, and DELETE against chronicler.episode_entities in application code, executed from whichever butler invokes the memory entity-merge tool (memory is enabled on 9 butlers). RFC 0010 permits only read-only, view-mediated, migration-tracked cross-schema access and says 'Write operations ... must always go through the Switchboard'; RFC 0014 sanctions only 'migration-tracked views' as chronicler's cross-schema read surface. No RFC covers a foreign module mutating chronicler's schema. With a single shared DB user (db.py:270-291) and search_path-only scoping (db.py:258-267), nothing at the database level prevents this either — doctrine's 'a butler cannot access another butler's schema' is enforced by convention alone.

findings.title: Direct cross-schema application-code reads in shared modules, without the RFC 0010-mandated view mechanism or any RFC
findings.detail: RFC 0010's mechanism guardrail requires 'a SQL view ..., not direct cross-schema queries in application code' plus migration-tracked grants, and the architecture doc's anti-pattern list bans 'cross-schema access without an RFC, explicit guardrails, and reuse criteria'. Yet: modules/memory/tools/writing.py:108,222 queries relationship.entity_predicate_registry inline; modules/approvals/email_guard.py:62 and modules/approvals/_shared.py:106 query relationship.entity_facts inline (running on whichever butler the approvals gate wraps, e.g. messenger); modules/contacts/backfill.py:165,190 and email_identity_matching.py:214 read relationship.entity_facts. None is view-mediated; none is documented as an exception. (Distinct from the in-flight contacts/entity-store retirement epic, which addresses which store holds identity, not the access mechanism.)

findings.title: Framework-to-roster dependency inversion: 16 src/ files import roster-defined butler code via an import-time sys.modules injection with swallowed failures

findings.title: Daemon core hard-depends on the approvals module: top-level import plus an inline pending_actions writer inside daemon.py
findings.detail: daemon.py:103 imports modules.approvals.gate.apply_approval_gates at top level and daemon.py:1333-1460 embeds approval-gating orchestration including a bespoke _enqueue_overlap_action that INSERTs pending_actions rows and imports approvals models/events inline (daemon.py:1442-1446). Approvals gating is de facto core policy implemented as a module, so core reaches into module internals instead of the module extending core. Same pattern for modules/pipeline.py: daemon.py:105 imports MessagePipeline directly and daemon.py:544 attaches it to 'modules that support set_pipeline()' — an ad-hoc protocol outside the Module ABC.

findings.title: Hardcoded content-classification regexes in the deterministic daemon routing path
findings.detail: roster/switchboard/tools/routing/classify.py bakes English keyword regexes for scheduling (:15-30), food/nutrition (:31-53), and retrospective intents into daemon code that biases routing decisions. audits.jarvis_gap: Today the repo has real cruft governance (epic bu-zquce closed 16/17 children; bundle-registry documents a delete-on-graduation policy) but no enforcement, so dead weight re-accumulates between manual passes faster than they run: ~3,000+ lines of orphaned frontend production code (a whole retired relationship UI, a pre-One-Spend costs pair, six dead hooks, a duplicated passport atom library whose tests pin non-shipping copies), live backend deprecation shims with zero remaining producers, a dual-column state representation in memory episodes, and an OpenSpec change lifecycle that ships code without checking tasks or archiving — the ideal state (every module load-bearing, one canonical copy of every utility, shims deleted the day their last producer dies, spec folders archived the day code merges) is reachable with one amnesty pass plus a knip-style CI gate and an archival step in the worker contract.
audits.ideal: A single-owner codebase where an automated import-graph gate (knip or equivalent) makes an unimported module a CI failure, every formatter/atom/util has exactly one home with tests pinned to the shipping copy, deprecation shims are deleted the moment their last producer is migrated (grep-verified, loud-fail otherwise), DB columns encode each fact exactly once with guarded drops for the losers, and the OpenSpec change lifecycle closes automatically — merged work checks its tasks and archives its change folder in the same PR — so cruft epics become unnecessary rather than recurring.

audits.jarvis_gap: The knowledge architecture's skeleton is genuinely strong — docs/README.md is a model synthesis, the five-pillar layout is coherent, module-system.md matches code, and zero dead relative links exist in docs/ — but accuracy discipline fails exactly on the highest-traffic, most load-bearing paths. The fresh-clone quickstart is broken (a postgres compose service that no longer exists is the documented first step in six places), the deployment topology map describes an April-era world (4 of 16 connectors, no chronicler, per-butler containers that were replaced by one butlers-up service, external-postgres/Garage/tailnet migration never propagated), the frontend spec set that declares itself "canonical source of truth for current dashboard behavior" with a same-change Update Rule contains 3.5-month-old claims that approvals is not a frontend surface and that the dashboard has four write endpoints, and — worst — the dual CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md butler prompt files have silently diverged so runtime behavior differs by which LLM CLI spawns: a Claude-runtime relationship session never sees the MANDATORY scope='relationship' filter rule. The ideal (every clause a door on an unbroken trace spine; failure never impersonating health) applies to docs too: today several docs impersonate authority they no longer have, and the 1,260-line append-only root AGENTS.md taxes every agent's context with verified-dead contracts.

findings.title: Butler prompt files (CLAUDE.md vs AGENTS.md) silently diverged — runtime behavior differs by LLM CLI

audits.jarvis_gap: All five pillars exist and are individually strong — doctrine (about/heart-and-soul, 7 non-negotiable rules, updated 06-28), 21 indexed RFCs with summaries, 177 openspec capability specs, topology maps, craft-and-care standards, and navigation skills installed for every pillar — which puts the architecture itself near the top of the maturity rubric. What is missing is the metabolism: there is no staleness machinery anywhere (zero last-reviewed metadata across about/ and docs/), the OpenSpec change lifecycle has decoupled from the beads fleet that actually ships work (shipped changes unarchived, tasks.md at 0/25 for merged features), a 1,260-line AGENTS.md has become a shadow contract layer holding ~150 normative "X contract" notes that belong in specs/RFCs, a declared spec rule (Source References) is dead law violated by 149/176 specs, and operationally dangerous facts (the prod/dev DB naming inversion) live only in private agent memories. The ideal one-hand instrument keeps its knowledge layers self-truing; today they true only when a human or audit run happens to look.

findings.title: AGENTS.md is a shadow spec layer: ~150 normative contracts live in agent scratch notes
findings.evidence: grep -c '^### ' AGENTS.md → 201 headings in a 1,260-line file; the majority are titled '<X> contract' and are normative wire/API/schema contracts, e.g. AGENTS.md:816 'Route.execute authn/authz contract', :836 'Approvals immutable event-log contract', :789 'Spawner system prompt composition contract', :759 'Route/notify envelope contract', :872 'Scheduler native-dispatch contract'. Per the five-pillar model (th-projects project-shape SKILL.md) contracts belong in openspec/ or about/legends-and-lore/, not in a memory-notes file with no review, ownership, or traceability chain.
findings.detail: These notes are load-bearing (agents read AGENTS.md before specs), unversioned as contracts, and silently fork the WHAT layer: a spec change that contradicts an AGENTS.md 'contract' note produces two competing normative sources. This is wrong-layer placement at scale, not individual drift (so not covered by bu-17axsl's spec-code reconciliation).

findings.title: Dead governance rule: 149/176 specs violate the mandated Source References section
findings.evidence: openspec/config.yaml rules.spec mandates '## Source References' listing doctrine rules + RFC numbers per spec; grep -rL 'Source References' openspec/specs/*/spec.md → 149 non-compliant vs 27 compliant. Same file: 'Design contracts: about/legends-and-lore/rfcs/ (12 accepted RFCs)' — 21 RFCs exist (ls about/legends-and-lore/rfcs | wc -l).
findings.detail: A rule no tooling enforces and 85% of the corpus ignores is dead doctrine — it also breaks the pillar traceability chain (doctrine→RFC→spec) that the Source References section was designed to carry. The stale '12 accepted RFCs' feeds wrong context into every OpenSpec generation run.

findings.title: OpenSpec change lifecycle has decoupled from the beads fleet that ships the work
findings.evidence: openspec/changes/switchboard-rule-promotion/tasks.md shows 0/25 tasks done, yet the feature merged (git log: 122f1fd50 'demotion via 1-in-K spot-check' #3015, ffb17289c 'rule promotion trigger job' #2999). memory-catalog-default-on is 5/5 [x] and shipped (07-04 epic move 15) but still in changes/ not archive/. attention-ledger-broker 13/15, decision-loop-one-tap-approvals 0/24 (epic bu-24lu6 executing). k3s-deployment-helm-chart untouched since 2026-03-22.
findings.detail: Work ships via beads epics; nobody runs apply→archive→sync on the corresponding OpenSpec change, so changes/ no longer signals what is active, and delta specs that should have folded into main specs sit as phantom authorities. The archive (132 entries) proves the lifecycle used to run. k3s change also contains an unexecuted architectural decision ('AGENTS.md writes moved to DB') that is invisible because the change is neither active nor parked.

findings.title: Operationally dangerous facts live only in agent memories, not durable docs
findings.evidence: The prod/dev DB naming inversion (butlers-db-dev is the LIVE system; butlers-db is empty) appears nowhere in about/ or docs/ except one archived change note: openspec/changes/archive/2026-06-12-entity-v3-lifecycle-and-depth/design.md:88 "'prod'/'dev' naming is reversed — see repo memory butlers-db-host-topology". about/lay-and-land/deployment.md (last commit 2026-04-08) has zero mention of the .env.dev/.env.prod split (grep -i 'env.dev|butlers-db' → no hits).
findings.detail: Lay-and-land owns deployment topology per the pillar model, yet the single fact most likely to cause a destructive migration against the wrong DB is discoverable only via a private per-user memory file that other agents and the owner's future selves cannot see. Same pattern class: Google OAuth credential topology and the contact/entity store split live primarily in memories/AGENTS.md.

findings.title: Rule 6 requires 'formal amendment' of governing documents but no amendment protocol exists and manifestos are stale by months
findings.evidence: about/heart-and-soul/vision.md:104-114 (Rule 6): governing documents are 'binding... must not be added without a formal amendment'. grep -ril 'amendment' about/ docs/index.md → no protocol document (only passing mentions in vision/architecture/design-language/security). Manifesto last-commit dates: roster/general 2026-02-10, roster/finance 2026-02-23, roster/travel 2026-02-23, roster/chronicler 2026-04-24 — finance predates RFC 0012's entire transaction data model era; chronicler predates the whole workday-visibility epic (bu-whhll, released 2026-07-05).
findings.detail: The system's own doctrine declares manifestos binding and formally amendable, but there is no mechanics doc (who drafts, owner adopts, downstream sweep) and the evidence shows amendments simply do not happen — capabilities grew massively with the governing documents frozen. Dead doctrine in the strict sense: a rule no process enforces.

findings.title: RFC status lifecycle unmaintained: vocabulary drift, no status column, statuses stale vs shipped reality
findings.evidence: about/legends-and-lore/README.md Conventions: 'Status values: Draft, Accepted, Deprecated' — actual headers include 'Proposed' (rfcs/0021:3), 'Rejected...Parked' (0019), 'Superseded by RFC 0004 Amendment 2' (0004). Index table (README.md:20-41) has no Status column; 0020/0021 statuses are buried in prose summaries. RFC 0021 still 'Proposed' while its epic bu-24lu6 is executing and the spec merged via PR #2840; RFC 0020 says 'Owner acceptance pending' while openspec/specs/calendar-overlay-aggregation exists.
findings.detail: The RFC index is otherwise excellent (summaries, reading order). The gap is purely lifecycle: statuses are written once and never trued against releases, and the convention's own vocabulary no longer matches usage.

findings.title: Evolving status/snapshot artifacts parked inside doctrine and topology pillars with no refresh process
findings.evidence: about/heart-and-soul/v1-status.md (338 lines): 'Last updated: 2026-06-28... as of commit 10c8a1bd6' — a per-commit status matrix inside the WHY layer, already ~2 weeks/dozens-of-PRs stale. about/lay-and-land/frontend-copy-inventory.md (3,248 lines): 'Auto-generated... Do not edit manually: re-run the script' — no scheduled regeneration exists, last run 2026-07-04. about/lay-and-land/detail-page-audit.md (849 lines) is a one-shot audit decision doc from 2026-05-06.
findings.detail: Status matrices and generated inventories are observational artifacts, not doctrine/topology; placing them in about/ pillars guarantees staleness-by-construction because nothing in the pillar maintenance model regenerates them. They also bloat the pillars agents are told to load selectively.

findings.title: Binding frontend doctrine lives in the guide layer and is 4 months stale
findings.evidence: docs/frontend/purpose-and-single-pane.md last commit 2026-03-21 (git log) — this run's own north-star document for UI surfaces. Its body still lists 'Approval queue and standing-rule governance... (target integration)' though approvals shipped long ago. Meanwhile the WHY of the dashboard is duplicated in about/heart-and-soul/design-language.md ('What the Dashboard Is', lines 28-42, four jobs) — two doctrine statements of dashboard purpose in two different layers, one frozen pre-Dispatch, pre-both-redesign-epics.
findings.detail: The frontend knowledge is split across five homes (heart-and-soul WHY, openspec dashboard-design-language WHAT, lay-and-land/frontend.md WHERE, docs/frontend/* guides, dispatch-kit HOW in a skill). The known design-language topology is deliberate; the NEW defect is that the doc treated as binding purpose-doctrine sits in docs/ (guides, unowned by any pillar skill) and has not been trued through two redesign epics.

findings.title: No spec catalog: 177 specs with no index, ownership, or staleness metadata
findings.evidence: ls openspec/specs | wc -l → 177 directories; ls openspec/specs | grep -i 'readme|index' → empty. Navigation exists only via .claude/skills/spec-and-spine/SKILL.md's naming-pattern heuristic ('core-*', 'butler-*', ...). No spec carries status/owner/last-verified metadata (spec.md headers are Purpose+Requirements only, e.g. openspec/specs/core-daemon/spec.md:1-8).
findings.detail: At 177 specs the corpus has outgrown filename navigation. The absence of any per-spec freshness signal is why known rot (the 'memory butler' phantom in 4 live specs) could only be found by an audit run rather than surfacing mechanically.

findings.title: AGENTS.md internally duplicated and self-contradictory

findings.title: Design-contract layer split across three homes with no admission criterion

findings.title: core-notify registration clause contradicts code: notify() is not registered for staffer butlers
findings.detail: Spec says 'Every butler daemon SHALL register a notify(...) MCP tool... audits.ideal: Every observable behavior in the fleet has exactly one current normative home: openspec/specs/ reads true against HEAD at all times because every behavior-changing PR ships its spec delta in the same change (already largely practiced) AND the archive/sync step runs as soon as a change's tasks complete, so stacked deltas never leave the main spec asserting falsehoods (required channel params, defer-only quiet hours, spot-check-free PolicyDecision). High-traffic infrastructure lanes — the switchboard classification path, runtime adapters, discretion honesty vocabulary — are held to the same spec bar as dashboard pages, since they are where silent drift costs the most. The reconciliation epic bu-17axsl has concrete sharded children with clause-level citations, and no normative-sounding document exists outside the five pillars.
audits.jarvis_gap: The governance machinery genuinely works in most lanes — secrets v2, purpose-tagged spend, delegation ledger, memory retention, and approvals triage all track code clause-for-clause, and deltas are written for most big lanes (attention ledger, rule promotion, chronicler distillation) — but the lifecycle stalls at its last step: at least five shipped-or-nearly changes sit unarchived, so the main specs for core-notify, ingestion-policy, and memory-discovery-catalog are materially false today, and one change (switchboard-rule-promotion) has 0/25 tasks ticked despite 5/7 beads merged. Meanwhile three infrastructure lanes shipped with no spec at all: the structured classification fast lane (the fleet's single most-trafficked decision path), the ApiAdapter runtime contract, and the discretion-hardening honesty vocabulary — plus notify()'s msg_context approval-gating behavior. bu-17axsl exists as the umbrella epic but has zero children, so none of this drift is scheduled work yet.

findings.title: Finance 'maintained without manual entry' rests solely on email-alert parsing; the marker has no primary data feed and its only roadmap home is an undecided proposal bead
findings.detail: vision.md's marker requires 'financial signals ... maintained without manual entry'. The finance butler's entire automatic inflow is Gmail receipt/bill/alert parsing (butler.toml: 'receipts, bills, subscriptions, and transaction alerts'); there is no transaction-feed connector in src/butlers/connectors/ (no simplefin/plaid/bank module). RFC 0012 defines a transaction data model, but the feed to fill it is parked inside bu-dyq22 ('Connector roadmap proposal', priority 2, feature, open) — a proposal bead, not a decided milestone, and it is itself one of the owner-attention items with no cadence (finding 1). Net: the financial leg of the four-domain marker is structurally the weakest of the four (health has chronicler feeders + Google Health; relationships has extraction pipeline + Dunbar scoring; calendar has bidirectional Google Calendar), and its unblocking is a decision-latency problem, not an engineering one. Reported as a governance finding, not a new connector proposal (bu-dyq22 owns that).

audits.ideal: Direction governance for a sovereign one-person JARVIS should close the loop from vision to measurement: the five success markers in vision.md each have a live, falsifiable gauge (days-since-intervention counter, routing-accuracy scoreboard from mined verdicts, per-domain no-manual-entry coverage, engagement-rate/ratchet telemetry, deploy-drift zero); v1-status.md refreshes on a cadence so every direction run starts from a warm baseline; parked ideas live in a discoverable ledger with unpark conditions; and — most importantly — owner decisions are first-class citizens of the system's own attention machinery: a decision desk surfaces every DECISION-REQUIRED bead with structured options and one-tap close, routed through the same attention ledger and Telegram inline keyboards the decision-loop epic is building for approvals, on a weekly review cadence, so nothing the fleet builds sits dark waiting for a choice nobody was asked to make.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today the knowledge architecture is genuinely strong (doctrine with non-negotiables, v1 ship/defer lists, 21 RFCs, an honest v1-status matrix, spec-traced epics) but the feedback loop from success markers back to work selection is broken in three places: the markers themselves are unmeasured (SC-6 and SC-8 'unproven' with no attestation mechanism, v1-status.md:167,204), the status matrix is 12 days stale across the two highest-velocity weeks ever, and the owner-decision queue — now 14 beads deep — has no cadence, no dashboard lane, and no attention-ledger coverage, so decision latency is actively degrading the flagship marker: production silently drops low-weight sender messages (bu-wzbu9 blocked on bu-v4ipc since 07-05) and five merged capabilities are dark behind an owner-gated 7-migration deploy (bu-zhfd0). Marker standing: 'weeks without intervention' — weakest (intervention debt compounding, deploy is manual ceremony, no intervention ledger); 'financial signals without manual entry' — weakest of the four domains (email-alert parsing only, feed parked in undecided bu-dyq22); 'frequency reduction on disengagement' — code-complete but dark/unmeasured; 'daily information flow' — functional but accuracy unattested (best benchmark 80.6% on non-primary model, not in CI); 'boring' — blocked on all of the above.

moves.title: Vertical 1 — Owner Decision Desk: decision beads as first-class attention citizens with a weekly review cadence

audits.jarvis_gap: Vision line 122 makes "runs for weeks without intervention" the first success marker; today the system demonstrably fails it and cannot even *know* it is failing. Production (butlers-dev) runs the dev hotreload compose profile off a live-mutating checkout with no deploy pipeline (the ghcr release workflow has never fired — zero git tags), which is the structural cause of the 7-revision migration gap (bu-zhfd0); every health signal (connector liveness, backup recency, butler heartbeat, Prometheus) is pull-only with no Alertmanager and no owner push, so connectors have died silently for 7+ weeks (bu-33dm2: offline since 2026-05-13); backups are daily but never restore-verified, hardcoded status="success", and live only on the daemon host; a host reboot silently drops the egress firewall and can resurrect the scaled-to-0 butlers-up via depends_on. The pieces of earned calm exist (restart policies, healthchecks, log retention, QA self-healing of sessions, restore scripts) but nothing closes the loop from infra failure to the owner's attention ledger, and nothing makes "what is deployed" a verifiable fact.

findings.title: Production runs the dev hotreload profile with no deploy pipeline — migration drift is structural, not accidental
findings.detail: The live stack replaces butlers-up with butlers-up-hotreload, which bind-mounts ./src and ./pyproject.toml from the fleet-mutated repo root and runs `uv sync --dev && exec uv run butlers up` at boot. Live code = whatever main was at the last container restart (uncontrolled, untagged); migrations run only from the separately-baked butlers-app:latest image via a one-shot service. Code advances continuously, the migration image does not — hence core_155..161 dark in prod (bu-zhfd0). The release.yml workflow (ghcr image on v* tags) has never fired: `git -C ~/gt/butlers tag` returns empty. There is no deployed-SHA record anywhere (no git_sha/GIT_COMMIT in src/butlers/api/ or Dockerfile; system.py only reports package __version__ at line 270-272). The k3s Helm openspec change exists but explicitly reuses this release pipeline and does not add deploy-state observability.
findings.evidence: docker-compose.yml:678-713 (hotreload mounts src, `uv sync --dev`), docker-compose.yml:106-113 (migrations from baked image); `git -C /home/tze/gt/butlers tag | tail -3` → empty; .github/workflows/release.yml (tag-triggered, dormant); grep git_sha/GIT_COMMIT over src/butlers/api/ + Dockerfile → only __version__ (src/butlers/api/routers/system.py:262-272); openspec/changes/k3s-deployment-helm-chart/proposal.md ('Existing Dockerfile and ghcr.io release pipeline reused')

findings.title: No watchdog-of-the-watchdogs: every infrastructure health signal is pull-only; infra death never reaches the owner
findings.detail: Connector liveness (online/stale/offline) is computed at API read time only; QA staffer discovery sources are log_scanner, session_records, tool_call_failures, butler_reports — no infra-state source; the observability stack has otel-collector/tempo/prometheus/grafana but no Alertmanager and no alert rules; no external deadman switch exists (grep healthchecks/deadman/watchdog finds only per-session watchdogs). The attention-ledger egress spine exists but nothing infra-shaped feeds it. Proven consequence: endpoints offline since 2026-05-13 and 2026-05-24, google_health 403 since 2026-06-07, all unnoticed for weeks until a manual audit (bu-33dm2, bu-whhll). If the daemon host reboots into a crash-loop or dies entirely, the dashboard dies with it and the owner learns nothing.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/ingestion_connectors.py:56-69,400,510-540 (liveness computed in the read path); src/butlers/core/qa/sources/ → butler_reports.py, log_scanner.py, session_records.py, tool_call_failures.py only; docker-compose.observability.yml services list (no alertmanager); `grep -rn healthchecks|deadman|watchdog src/ scripts/ docs/operations/` → session/bridge watchdogs only; bd show bu-33dm2 (offline since 2026-05-13/24)

findings.title: Backups are never verified, report hardcoded success, and have no off-host copy
findings.detail: backup-cron runs pg_dump daily into the local docker volume butlers_backups (14-day retention). The dashboard BackupFacts scanner fabricates health: every BackupEvent is emitted with status="success" purely because a file exists (system.py:454) — a truncated or logically-corrupt dump reads green, directly violating the 'failure never impersonates health' doctrine. scripts/pg_restore.sh + pg_verify_restore.sh exist but are a manual 'operator restore drill' (docs/operations/backup-restore.md) that nothing schedules; no table records a verified restore. Dumps live only on the daemon host — no S3/Garage offsite step despite S3 already in the topology (s3-blob-storage spec, migrate_blobs_to_s3.py). And when dumps silently stop, nothing pushes: staleness is visible only if the owner opens the system page.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/system.py:447-456 (status="success" hardcoded); deploy/backup/pg_dump.sh (local dir only, no offsite); docker-compose.yml:176-203 (backup-cron → butlers_backups volume); scripts/pg_restore.sh header ('Designed for the operator restore drill'); grep backup over roster/*/butler.toml + qa sources → no scheduled verification

findings.title: Host reboot silently degrades the stack: egress firewall lost, boot depends on `uv sync --dev`, and the scale-0 butlers-up trap
findings.detail: (1) egress-firewall.sh inserts iptables DOCKER-USER rules and is applied only by the compose.sh launcher (line 393) — no persistence (no iptables-save/netfilter-persistent, no systemd unit anywhere in the repo), no runtime verification, no dashboard surface; after reboot Docker auto-restarts all containers (restart: unless-stopped) but the egress network runs unfirewalled to LAN/tailnet until a human re-runs the script. (2) Both butlers-up and butlers-up-hotreload entrypoints run `uv sync --dev` before exec — daemon boot at 3am depends on lockfile state of the mutating repo and potentially PyPI reachability; a dependency merged to main between restarts changes what boots. (3) butlers-up-hotreload has depends_on: butlers-up: service_healthy while butlers-up is deliberately scaled to 0 in the live deployment — any plain `docker compose up -d` (or post-reboot reconcile) resurrects the wrong daemon or deadlocks the right one (hazard already bitten in bu-zhfd0, but only documented as tribal knowledge, never fixed structurally with a prod profile).
findings.evidence: scripts/compose.sh:393-395 (firewall applied by launcher only); scripts/egress-firewall.sh (no persistence mechanism, grep netfilter-persistent/iptables-save → none); docker-compose.yml:550, 681 (`uv sync --dev &&` in entrypoints); docker-compose.yml:706-712 (hotreload depends_on butlers-up service_healthy); docs/operations/docker-deployment.md → zero mentions of reboot/systemd/boot

findings.title: Post-outage cron catch-up fires every overdue task at once with stale intent and no staleness policy
findings.detail: tick() cron pass selects all rows WHERE enabled AND next_run_at <= now() and dispatches each — after a multi-hour/day host outage, every butler fires its full overdue schedule immediately on boot: a 7am 'morning digest' prompt fires at 4pm with no annotation that it is 9 hours late (known freelancing amplifier per the calendar 'Run butler event' incident), and a dozen simultaneous LLM spawns spike spend at the worst moment (cold boot). There is no per-task catchup/staleness policy — only paused/quarantined butlers get the drop-not-queue semantics (dispatch gate), and that path drops crons with just a logger.info, never telling the owner their scheduled tasks are being discarded indefinitely while a butler sits stale.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/scheduler.py:1988-1999 (unbounded `next_run_at <= $1` fetch, no staleness filter or late-fire annotation); scheduler.py:1945-1953 (gate drops ticks with logger.info only); scheduler.py:1886-1893 (drop-not-queue documented only for the gated path)

moves.title: Per-task catch-up policy for scheduled tasks (time-staleness semantics)
moves.why: Distinct new design vs the known 'precondition gates' carryover (that gates on data preconditions; this is wall-clock staleness): give scheduled_tasks a catchup_policy — 'always' | 'skip_if_older_than: <window>' | 'never' — consulted in tick()'s cron pass, so a 7am digest missed by 9 hours records last_result='skipped_stale' (honest, visible in the scheduler UI) instead of firing with stale intent, and any late fire that does run gets a '[Late fire: scheduled 07:00, dispatching 16:12]' prompt prefix so the runtime LLM can't freelance off a wrong time assumption (root cause class of the calendar 'Run butler event' double-dispatch incident). Also caps cold-boot spend spikes after outages. Payoff: scheduled tasks 'fire on time... and recover from transient failures' (vision success marker) with recovery that is policy, not stampede.

Set skip windows on the obvious daily-digest tasks across roster/*/butler.toml.
